papers.title: Fixed points via tilting
papers.abstract: In this article we initiate the study of perfect commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in the non-connective setting. As an application we show that given a finite $C_p$-space $X$ the $\mathbb{F}_p$-cochains on $X^{C_p}$ can be recovered as a base-change of the tilt of the Tate construction on cochains on $X^e$.

papers.title: Motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces at the characteristic
papers.abstract:
We provide a novel, homotopy theoretic model for the motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces $K(Z_{(p)}(n), 2n) \in Spc(k)$ over fields of characteristic p. Using this, we determine their motives and, consequently, determine the motivic Steenrod algebra at the characteristic. Applications include the Hopkins--Morel isomorphism over arbitrary base schemes as well as the computation of the p-completed motivic stable stems and algebraic cobordism groups of fields of characteristic p.
  Along the way we expand the theory of normed algebraic structures in motivic homotopy theory, compare them to derived algebra at the characteristic, and produce a functor computing the motivic homology of the $P^1$-loop spaces of (certain) motivic spaces in terms of the motives.

papers.title: On closed symmetric monoidal enriched $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We show that a closed symmetric monoidal V-enriched $\infty$-category can be described by a lax symmetric monoidal functor to V from its underlying $\infty$-category.

papers.title: The Derived Auslander--Iyama Correspondence II: Bimodule Calabi--Yau Structures
papers.abstract: Let $d$ be a positive integer. In a previous article we established a bijective correspondence between the following classes of objects, considered up to the appropriate notion of equivalence: differential graded algebras (dg) with finite-dimensional $0$-th cohomology such that the canonical generator of their perfect derived category is a basic $d\ZZ$-cluster tilting object, and basic Frobenius algebras that are twisted $(d+2)$-periodic as bimodules. In this article, we prove a variant of our general correspondence for bimodule right Calabi--Yau dg algebras. A novel ingredient is a new cohomology theory which contains obstructions to the existence and uniqueness of minimal $A_\infty$-bimodule structures on a graded bimodule. As an application of our results, we obtain, to our knowledge, the first example of an algebraic triangulated category with a triangulated Calabi--Yau structure that cannot be lifted to a bimodule right Calabi--Yau structure on any of its dg enhancements.

papers.title: Unfolding of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
papers.abstract: We prove Lurie's proposed description of left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories in terms of purely $\infty$-categorical data. More precisely, unfolding gives an equivalence between left rigid symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories and complete categorical chain complexes of rigid symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories. More generally, unfolding identifies skeletal sequences with categorical chain complexes without the completeness condition. We extend these equivalences to $(\infty,\infty)$-categories and, stably, obtain an equivalence between complete unbounded categorical chain complexes and left rigid categorical spectra. We also analyze their groupoid completion and express the homotopy groups of the associated spaces and spectra in terms of categorical cycles and boundaries. As examples, we construct the categorical chain complexes associated to geometric and algebraic bordism categories, including their equivariant variants, and to iterated span categories. Their localizations recover classical bordism and $L$-groups, while the span examples are related to algebraic $K$-theory.

papers.title: $S_n$-equivariant $L$-classes of Cartesian powers of Witt spaces and the Hodge index conjecture for symmetric products
papers.abstract: For a compact oriented even-dimensional Witt pseudomanifold $X$, we compute the $S_n$-equivariant Banagl--Zagier $L$-classes of $X^n$ in terms of the Goresky--MacPherson $L$-classes of $X$ and the intersection cohomology Euler characteristic of $X$. This generalizes a theorem of Zagier for manifolds. Our approach is based on analyzing the equivariant structure of the signature operator of $X^n$ using equivariant $KK$-theory and power operations in analytic $K$-homology. We establish an analytic $K$-homology analogue of Moonen's algebraic localization theorem by proving that the localized Chern character of the $n$-th power operation, evaluated at an $n$-cycle, agrees with the $n$-th homological Adams operation applied to the Chern character. As an application, we prove that the characteristic class Hodge index conjecture for singular varieties, formulated by Brasselet--Sch\"urmann--Yokura, is preserved under taking symmetric products of complex projective varieties.

papers.title: A sphere-product counterexample to the additivity of homology nilpotency
papers.abstract: Homology nilpotency need not increase under a product with a sphere. We construct a simply connected, closed smooth manifold $M$ of dimension $53$, rationally elliptic with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(\pi_*(M)\otimes\mathbb Q\bigr)=7$, such that $cat_0(M)=10$ and $Hnil(M\times S^2)=Hnil(M)=11$. The inequality $Hnil(X\times Y)\leq Hnil(X)+Hnil(Y)$ can therefore be strict even for a product of a closed manifold with $S^2$ as the second factor.

papers.title: Absolute descent and the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem
papers.abstract:
We continue the programme developed in Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory by studying descent for augmented pseudocosimplicial objects. Let $\mathcal H$ be a $2$-category, and let $\operatorname{suc}=\mathsf{1}+(-)$ be the successor monad on the augmented simplex category. Precomposition with $\operatorname{suc}$ induces the d\'ecalage pseudomonad $\mathbb S$ on the $2$-category of augmented pseudocosimplicial objects with values in $\mathcal H$. We prove that every successor contraction makes the corresponding augmented pseudocosimplicial object effective for descent. This structure is preserved by postcomposition with every pseudofunctor. Consequently, the resulting descent object is an absolute bilimit.
  A first application concerns split epimorphisms. We recover the Janelidze--Tholen characterization of absolute effective descent morphisms given in Facets of Descent II. Moreover, we prove that one direction holds for every pseudofunctor $A\colon C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal H$, where $\mathcal H$ is an arbitrary $2$-category.
  Consequently, every $\mathbb S$-pseudoalgebra is of absolute descent. In particular, this holds for every free $\mathbb S$-pseudoalgebra, and hence for every one-sided d\'ecalage. This makes the shift-effectiveness hypothesis in the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem of Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory automatic. Thus, under the adjointness and Beck--Chevalley hypotheses, the descent and Eilenberg--Moore factorizations are equivalent whenever they exist. We thus obtain a stronger version of the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem for arbitrary augmented pseudocosimplicial objects, which we call the formal B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem. Applied to indexed \v{C}ech objects associated with pseudofunctors $A\colon C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal H$, this theorem extends the classical B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem to an arbitrary $2$-category $\mathcal H$.

papers.title: Koszul duality for boundary categories
papers.abstract: We study how Koszul duality relates two kinds of boundary constructions associated with a smooth category and a proper category. For a smooth category with a proper Koszul-dualizing subcategory, we construct a fully faithful functor from its categorical neighborhood of infinity to the singularity category associated to the proper category. We prove that this functor is an equivalence precisely when the smooth category is reflexive, meaning that it can be reconstructed from its finite-dimensional module theory. Under a Gorenstein condition, satisfied in the Calabi--Yau setting, the functor is induced by restriction of modules. We give algebraic criteria that ensure equivalence and obtain an identification of Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
papers.abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: Du Bois cohomology of noncommutative spaces and the Hodge numbers invariance conjecture for singular varieties
papers.abstract:
We extend the definition of cdh-sheafified Hochschild homology from varieties to stable categories linear over a field of characteristic zero, thereby proving its Morita-invariance. The dimensions of its homology groups give meaningful numerical invariants of a category; we combine them with invariants coming from topological K-theory and Poincar\'e duality to prove equality of mixed Hodge numbers for singular complex projective Fourier--Mukai partners in several classes in dimensions two, three, and four, including normal surfaces and threefolds with rational singularities and equal irregularity.
  Beyond these applications, we construct Du Bois versions of topological cyclic homology of stable categories together with appropriate multiplicative structures, prove a Geller--Weibel-type result for the variants of negative cyclic homology we introduce, and give categorical characterizations of cohomological purity of proper varieties and the $\mathbb{Q}$-factoriality defect of complex projective threefolds with rational singularities.

papers.title: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.

papers.title: Indecomposable Uniform Families on the Adams 4-Line
papers.abstract: We show that the $f_j$, $p_j$, $D_3(j)$, and $p_j'$ families on the 4-line of the classical Adams spectral sequence all conform to the Uniform Doomsday Conjecture. We do so by first using Bruner's formula to establish uniform families of differentials on these classes. We then study the Burklund-Xu and Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences to ensure that the differential targets are nonzero. The $f_j$ family requires further analysis of possible Adams $d_2$ differentials since the $f_j$ support uniform $d_3$ differentials. As a result of our work, only two indecomposable $\text{Sq}^0$ families remain to be settled in Adams filtration 4.

papers.title: On the representability of actions of algebras with several bilinear multiplications
papers.abstract: We study the representability of actions in varieties of algebras with $n \geq 1$ not necessarily associative bilinear multiplications. We first prove that, for homogeneous varieties, action accessibility is equivalent to being an Orzech category of interest. For an action accessible, operadic variety we then construct the external weak actor $\mathcal{E}(X)$ of an algebra $X$, an algebra with $n$ bilinear partial operations together with a natural monomorphism encoding the actions on $X$. We characterise the algebras admitting an actor in terms of $\mathcal{E}(X)$, and we deduce an obstruction to action representability: if, for some algebra $X$ with trivial multiplications, $\mathcal{E}(X)$ does not satisfy a multilinear identity of the variety, then the variety is not action representable. Computing the external weak actor explicitly, we obtain that associative and matching dialgebras are weakly action representable but not action representable, and that Poisson algebras, left-right non-commutative Poisson algebras and matching Lie algebras are not action representable. Finally, we introduce the reduced type $(p,q)$ of such a variety and prove that, over a field of characteristic different from $2$, an operadic variety of reduced type $(p,0)$, $(0,q)$ or $(1,1)$ is action representable if and only if it is term equivalent to the variety of Lie algebras or to that of abelian algebras. For the reduced types $(p,0)$ and $(0,q)$, the arguments require no assumption on the cardinality of the field, whereas the case $(1,1)$ requires the field to be infinite.

papers.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
papers.abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.

papers.title: A Directed Cubical Framework for k-critical Bipersistence Modules
papers.abstract: In topological data analysis, multiparameter persistence modules (MPMs) are used to analyze data with multiple parameters. Summarizing topological information for MPMs is a non-trivial task; one useful summary of bipersistence modules is the fibered barcode \cite{lesnick2015interactive,lesnick2025fast}. In this paper, we use a directed topological construction of the parameter space of a bifiltration to extend the fibered barcode. Specifically, given a $k$-critical bifiltration $F$, we build an associated directed Euclidean cubical complex $C$ whose directed paths each correspond to a one-parameter subfiltration of $F$. The path space of $C$, $\di{C}$, is used to define the \emph{extended fibered barcode}, which contains all possible monotonically increasing paths in $C$. We show that there can be paths in $\di{C}$ which generate filtrations not obtainable along a line with positive slope, and that all lines with positive slope have a path in $\di{C}$ that generate an equivalent barcode. We introduce two types of equivalence for these restricted modules: combinatorial equivalence of diagrams, and simplicial equivalence of the filtrations generating the modules. We show that removing certain cubes from $C$ yields a subcomplex on which dihomotopic paths induce simplicially equivalent filtrations, and hence combinatorially equivalent diagrams.

papers.title: A result of continuous stability for generalized persistence diagrams
papers.abstract: We study persistence modules obtained from the $A$-fundamental groupoids of finite graphs. Moreover, we verify the categorical properties needed to form generalized persistence diagrams, and describe a quotient that identifies equivalent groupoids. A normalized linear presheaf construction places these modules in an essentially small abelian category, where Patel's Continuity Theorem gives a $1$-Lipschitz estimate in erosion distance. Explicit graph filtrations illustrate the groupoid-valued construction, and so we suggest a new approach to interpret persistence diagrams and large data sets in topological data analysis, based on recent works of A-homotopy theory of the last years.

papers.title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
papers.abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

papers.title: Cohomology of regular spherical actions
papers.abstract: We study regular spherical actions, namely, actions of a connected compact Lie group G on a manifold M with equidimensional orbits, some of which are spheres. These spherical orbits are diffeomorphic to homogeneous spaces G/H, and there is a list of nine possible families of pairs (G, H). The normalizer N of H in G plays an important role in our calculations, as does the Weyl group W = N/H. In fact, there are three possibilities for W, namely: Z_2, S^1 and S^3. The goal of this paper is to relate the cohomology of M to that of the orbit space M/G. We obtain a particularly simple relationship in the first case, W = Z_2. For the remaining two cases, W = S^1 and W = S^3, it is already known that the cohomology of M and that of the orbit space M/G are related by the Gysin sequence ... \to H^k(M/G) \to H^k(M ) \to H^{k-d}(M/G) \to H^{k+1}(M/G) \to ... In this work, we provide a direct construction of this sequence, avoiding the use of spectral sequences. Moreover, we give an explicit description of the connecting homomorphism as multiplication by a power of the Euler class associated with the action of the Weyl group W = S^l on the fixed-point set M^H.

papers.title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
papers.abstract:
We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations.
  The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to torsion-freeness in the $K$-theory of crystallographic group $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to a question of S\'anchez Salda\~na--Vel\'asquez and L\"uck asking whether the topological K-theory of the reduced group C*-algebra of a split crystallographic group with finite cyclic holonomy is always torsion-free. For two explicit split crystallographic groups with translation subgroup of rank four and holonomy of order four, we compute the equivariant K-theory of the classifying space for proper actions and find nontrivial two-torsion. The equivariant universal coefficient theorem transfers this torsion to proper equivariant K-homology, and the Baum--Connes conjecture identifies the resulting groups with the topological K-theory of the corresponding reduced group C*-algebras.

papers.title: $AV$-modules on affine algebraic groups
papers.abstract: We study $AV$-modules on an affine algebraic group $G$, that is, modules that admit compatible actions of the algebra of regular functions on $G$ and the Lie algebra of vector fields. A central role in this theory is played by the Lie algebra of jets of vector fields. Our main result is the Decomposition Theorem for the Lie algebra of jets of vector fields. We apply the Decomposition Theorem to describe differentiable $AV$-modules on $G$.

papers.title: A Bound Helium Dianion Does Not Exist
papers.abstract: For a non-relativistic atom with $Z$ protons and $N$ bound electrons, Lieb proved in 1984 that $N<2Z+1$. Several improved bounds have been developed, but they all leave open the question of whether a bound helium dianion can exist. We prove that the answer is no. The ground-state energies of the four- and three-electron helium Hamiltonians coincide, $E_4(Z{=}2)=E_3(Z{=}2)$, so a helium nucleus binds at most three electrons. A weighted form of Lieb's identity reduces the problem to the nonnegativity of an explicit two-electron Schrodinger operator $m$, and Barta's inequality further reduces it to the pointwise nonnegativity of an explicit function of three variables. We prove the nonnegativity of this function by a combination of analytic estimates and a computer-assisted certification in interval arithmetic, and we publish the certificate with the paper.

papers.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
papers.abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

papers.title: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers
  of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere.
  Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves
  $
  X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x),
  $
  where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$
  has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$.
  After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$,
  the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic
  if its Newton polygon is minimal
  as $f$ varies over all Laurent
  polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$.
  For $p$ sufficiently large relative to $d_1$ and $d_2$,
  we construct a combinatorial cost polygon $GL(d_1,d_2,p)$
  and prove that its attainment is characterized by the nonvanishing
  of a homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of $f$.
  Moreover, we prove that these conditions stabilize:
  there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U$
  in the coefficient space that is defined over $\Q$
  and depends only on $d_1$ and $d_2$,
  whereby for any $f$ whose coefficients lie in
  $U(\overline{\Q})$,
  the reduction is generic at every prime ideal above sufficiently large
  rational primes, and for every rank $\ell$ permitted by the residue field.
  This result extends Zhu's result for one ramification point.

papers.title: A Known M-Curve of Degree 8 in OSCAR
papers.abstract: We show how the computer algebra system OSCAR can be used to retrace geometric constructions of plane algebraic curves and provide topologically correct and visually pleasing drawings. The approach is illustrated on Shustin's construction from 1987 of a particular M-curve of degree eight. We arrive at an explicit homogeneous trivariate polynomial with rational coefficients, and we provide a computational proof of all claimed properties of Shustin's original article.

papers.title: A Microlocal Theory for Zariski-Constructible Sheaves on Rigid Analytic Varieties
papers.abstract: We develop a microlocal theory, in the sense of Kashiwara-Schapira, for Zariski-constructible sheaves on rigid analytic varieties. We define and study monodromic sheaves, the monodromic Fourier transform, specialisation, microlocalisation, micro-hom, and singular support in this context. Some questions and conjectures are formulated in the end. The appendix contains infinity-categorical characterisations of monodromic sheaves.

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(\Lambda^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-mod})\), without imposing finiteness conditions on \(\Lambda^!\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_{\lambda})\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, thereby closing a gap left open in the work of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

papers.title: A note on toric periods in unramified families
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the algebra $\mathbf{C}[X_1^{\pm 1},X_2^{\pm 1}]$ and $Q(A)$ its quotient field. In this short article we exhibit the correct normalization for the toric period on the parabolically induced unramified family over $Q(A)$, so that it behaves optimally under restriction to the parabolically induced unramified family over $A$. Finally, we explicitly describe the structure of the $A$-module given by the image of this normalized period. These results answer questions raised by D. Prasad, and point towards potential generalizations to a broader unramified Gan-Gross-Prasad setting.

papers.title: A proof of the Zariski closure conjecture and quasi-Frobenius exponential algebras
papers.abstract: Let $G=\exp(\g)$ be an exponential solvable Lie group, $\pi\in\widehat G$, and $\Omega_\pi$ the coadjoint orbit attached to $\pi$ by the orbit method. The Zariski closure conjecture asserts that the Poisson characteristic variety $\VA(\pi_\nu)$ of the deformed representation coincides with the Zariski closure of $\Omega_\pi$ in $\g^*$. Known until now only in special situations, including the nilpotent case, it is proved here in full generality. Since the Hilbert space of $\pi$ is a quantization of the symplectic manifold $\Omega_\pi$, the statement says that the passage back from the representation to the orbit, a dequantization, loses nothing: the orbit is recovered, up to Zariski closure, from the algebra alone. We also characterize the quasi-Frobenius exponential Lie algebras, those whose dual vector space is a Zariski-dense coadjoint orbit, through the triviality of the annihilator of an irreducible representation.

papers.title: A Reider-type theorem for syzygies of cyclic covers of anticanonical rational surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $\pi\colon X\to S$ be a smooth ramified cyclic cover of an anticanonical rational surface, with $\kappa(X)\geq0$, and let $A$ be a divisor on $S$. We prove a Reider-type theorem for syzygies: for every integer $p\ge 0$, the adjoint divisor $K_X+\pi^*A$ satisfies Property $\mathrm{N}_p$ provided that $A\cdot C\geq p+3$ for every curve $C\subseteq S$ with $C^2\le 1$. One ingredient is a syzygy criterion for finite covers that reduces the weight-two Koszul vanishing on $X$ to weight-one vanishing for the nontrivial character modules on $S$. The most delicate case, in which $\dim|-K_S|=0$ and $K_S^2<0$, is handled by a separate geometric argument.

papers.title: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.

papers.title: A resolution of the Steinberg module of a parabolic subgroup of GL_n
papers.abstract: Let F be a field, G = GL_n(F), and let St be the Steinberg module of G. For a parabolic subgroup P of G, let St_P be its Steinberg module. There is a natural map rho_P: St -> St_P corresponding to intersection of a modular symbol with the Borel--Serre boundary. We construct a ZP-resolution Sh_P of St_P, the P-sharbly resolution. We also construct a P-equivariant chain map from the sharbly resolution of St to the P-sharbly resolution of St_P which enables us to compute the map induced on Steinberg homologies by rho_P. In the case when F is a number field and Gamma subset G is a torsion-free arithmetic subgroup, rho_P induces the restriction map H^(Gamma, E) -> H^(Gamma cap P, E) via Borel--Serre duality, for any coefficient module E which is flat over the base ring. If E is a vector space over Z/pZ this provides a computation of the restriction map on cohomology from Gamma to Gamma cap P in terms of sharblies, which enables the study of this restriction map in characteristic p, where Eisenstein series cannot be used.

papers.title: A Simple Categorical Calculus of Interacting Processes
papers.abstract: We present a calculus that models a simple sort of process interaction. Our calculus consists of a collection of terms together with a rewrite relation, parameterised by an arbitrary multicategory whose morphisms we understand as non-interactive processes. We show that our calculus is confluent and terminating, and that terms modulo the induced convertibility relation form a virtual double category. We relate our calculus to the free cornering of a monoidal category, which is a double-categorical model of process interaction that is similar in spirit to the calculus presented herein. Precisely, we construct a functor from the virtual double category given by our calculus into the underlying virtual double category of the free cornering of the free monoidal category on the multicategory of non-interacting processes. If we think of the terms of our calculus as programs and the rewriting system as an operational semantics for these programs, this functor gives a sound denotational semantics for our calculus in terms of the free cornering.

papers.title: Algebraically trivial automorphisms of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds
papers.abstract: Given an irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS) manifold $X$, we call an automorphism $f$ of $X$ algebraically trivial if $f$ acts trivially on the N\'eron--Severi group of $X$. In this paper, we extend the approach of Brandhorst--Cattaneo to classify, by means of lattice data, all the pairs $(X, G)$, where $X$ is an IHS manifold of a known deformation type (to this date), and $G$ is a finite group consisting of algebraically trivial automorphisms of $X$ that are nonsymplectic. In particular, we classify even-order algebraically trivial nonsymplectic automorphisms, with or without trivial discriminant action. In the case of nontrivial discriminant actions, we show that such automorphisms only exist for finitely many deformation types and orders

papers.title: Artinian reduction applied to the Largest Intersection Problem
papers.abstract: Suppose we have $r$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^m$ of degree $d$, whose defining polynomials are linearly independent and whose intersection is zero-dimensional. What is the maximum number of points in their intersection? This problem is motivated by computing the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, and a conjectured formula for this maximum was given in [21]. We prove the conjectured formula for arbitrary $m$ when $\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{d+2}{2}<r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}$. We use the notion of Artinian reduction to reformulate the problem in terms of graded Artinian algebras and then apply combinatorial tools to bound their Hilbert functions.

papers.title: Auslander-type grade conditions and subcategories related to syzygy modules
papers.abstract: The question of when a syzygy module or a module satisfying a Serre condition satisfies the cohomological vanishing conditions known as higher torsionfreeness has been extensively studied. In this paper, we address these questions using grade conditions introduced and studied by Auslander-Bridger and Auslander-Reiten. We also investigate homological conditions on Ext modules and, as an application, give a partial answer over commutative rings to a question of Auslander-Bridger concerning whether higher reflexive modules are higher torsionfree.

papers.title: Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce avalanche homology as a new (di)graph homology theory, based on the dynamics of the sandpile model. Avalanche homology is the simplicial homology of the avalanche complex generated from the sets of unstable vertices at the time steps of the sandpile dynamics. In this work we focus on digraphs, and our main results give the homotopy types of the avalanche complex for directed paths and directed cycles for certain initial configurations of the sandpile dynamics. Even for such simple digraphs a wide range of topologies can arise, and we compare this to the directed flag complex and to the recently introduced burning homology. Furthermore, the dynamics yields very naturally a filtered simplicial complex, and hence persistent avalanche homology.

papers.title: Base Change Of Fundamental Group Schemes
papers.abstract: Let $K/k$ be a field extension, $X$ a connected quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over $k$ with a rational point $x$, $p:X_K\to X$ the natural projection, $\mathcal{C}_X$ and $\mathcal{C}_{X_K}$ the Tannakian categories whose objects consist of vector bundles on $X$ and $X_K$ respectively. We give criteria for the natural homomorphism $\pi(\mathcal C_{X_K},x_K)\to\pi(\mathcal C_X,x)_K$ to be an isomorphism. Suppose further $X$ is geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$. As applications, we prove base change isomorphisms for $\pi^{\acute{e}t},\pi^{E\acute{e}t}$ under arbitrary extensions and for $\pi^S,\pi^N,\pi^{EN}$ under arbitrary algebraic extensions; a cuspidal cubic curve example shows that it can fail for purely transcendental extensions. In positive characteristic, base change isomorphism holds for $\pi^{Loc}$ and $\pi^{ELoc}$ under separable algebraic extensions; an elliptic curve example shows that it can fail for finite purely inseparable extensions.

papers.title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
papers.abstract: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.

papers.title: Building blocks for $W$-algebras of classical types
papers.abstract: The universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,3,4,\dots)$ serves as a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,3,\dots,N)$ for some $N$ in the sense that under mild hypothesis, all such vertex algebras arise as quotients of $W_{\infty}$. There is an $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ family of such $1$-parameter vertex algebras which, after tensoring with a Heisenberg algebra, are known as $Y$-algebras. They were introduced by Gaiotto and Rap\v{c}\'ak and are expected to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras in type $A$, i.e., every $W$-(super) algebra in type $A$ is an extension of a tensor product of finitely many $Y$-algebras. Similarly, the orthosymplectic $Y$-algebras are $1$-parameter quotients of a universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,4,6,\dots)$, which is a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,4,\dots, 2N)$ for some $N$. Unlike type $A$, these algebras are not all the building blocks for $W$-algebras of types $B$, $C$, and $D$. In this paper, we construct a new universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra of type $W(1^3, 2, 3^3, 4, 5^3,6,\dots)$ which we denote by $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ since it contains a copy of the affine vertex algebra $V^k(\mathfrak{sp}_2)$. We identify $8$ infinite families of $1$-parameter quotients of $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ which are analogues of the $Y$-algebras. We regard $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ as a fundamental object on equal footing with $W_{\infty}$ and $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$, and we give some heuristic reasons for why we expect the $1$-parameter quotients of these three objects to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras of classical types. Finally, we prove that $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ has many quotients which are strongly rational. This yields new examples of strongly rational $W$-superalgebras.

papers.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
papers.abstract: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.

papers.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
papers.abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.

papers.title: Canonical quantum curve I
papers.abstract:
We formulate a canonical quantum curve conjecture $\widehat H\Psi_*=0$ for spectral curves of positive genus. Here $\Psi_*$ is the non-perturbative wave function associated with Eynard--Orantin topological recursion, specialized at the \emph{canonical vanishing point}, a distinguished zero of the closed non-perturbative partition function. The operator $\widehat H$ is obtained by Weyl quantization of $H(x,y)$, with $\widehat x=x\cdot$ and $\widehat y=\hbar\partial_x$, together with quantum corrections to its coefficients. These corrections depend only on closed moduli and $\hbar$ and vanish classically. Whenever a geometric definition is available, we conjecture that the corrected coefficients are suitably normalized Wilson-loop expectation values. When a corresponding refined theory exists, we conjecture a relation between the canonical vanishing point and the closed Nekrasov--Shatashvili free energy.
  We prove the quantum curve conjecture for Weierstrass curves and the mirror curves of canonical bundles of smooth projective toric weak del Pezzo surfaces, including local $\mathbb P^2$. For the local surfaces considered here, we relate the canonical vanishing point to a derivative of the closed NS free energy. For local $\mathbb P^2$, we also identify the corrected coefficient with a suitably normalized, geometrically defined NS Wilson-loop expectation value.

papers.title: Cartesian closedness of lax comma categories
papers.abstract: For a finitely complete category X, we prove that the lax comma category Cat//X is cartesian closed if and only if its free coproduct completion Fam(X) is cartesian closed. The proof uses a change-of-base theorem: postcomposition with a functor induces a left adjoint between lax comma categories precisely when that functor is a left multiadjoint. We describe the exponentials and derive examples from known results on family categories.

papers.title: Categorification of $k$-Schur functions and refined Macdonald positivity
papers.abstract:
We establish a substantial part of the categorification framework for $k$-Schur functions proposed in Chen's Ph.D.\ thesis, written under the supervision of Mark Haiman. More precisely, we realize $k$-Schur functions as the graded characters of a distinguished family of objects in a certain module category and establish module-theoretic analogues of several foundational properties of $k$-Schur functions. A final part of Chen's framework predicts a homological characterization of modules admitting filtrations by these distinguished objects; we establish this characterization under an additional combinatorial hypothesis.
  In addition, we unconditionally prove that modules arising in this framework admit filtrations whose subquotients are affine Demazure modules of level $k$. As a consequence, modified Macdonald polynomials expand positively in the characters of affine Demazure modules. This may be viewed as a homological refinement of Macdonald positivity, arising from an intrinsic $\mathrm{ext}$-orthogonality condition on the corresponding Garsia--Haiman modules. We also prove the combinatorial hypothesis for $m \le 2k$ in the appendix and verify it computationally for $m\leq 19$, yielding $k$-Schur positivity of modified Macdonald polynomials in these cases.
  Our approach builds on our previous work on the algebraic and geometric realization of Catalan symmetric functions, a class encompassing both $k$-Schur and Hall--Littlewood functions.

papers.title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
papers.abstract: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

papers.title: Characterization of the boundary zero set of stable polynomials in $\mathbb B_2$
papers.abstract: Given a polynomial $p\in \mathbb{C}[z,w]$ whose zeros lie outside the unit ball $\mathbb{B}_2$ of $\mathbb{C}^2,$ we study its local Weierstrass polynomial--obtained via the Weierstrass Preparation Theorem--and provide a strong version of the Nash curve selection lemma. These results lead to a characterization of the intersection of the zero set of $p$ with the unit sphere: $\mathcal{Z}(p)\cap\mathbb{S}_{2}.$

papers.title: Closed energy formulas on tensor squares of perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$
papers.abstract: For each integer $l\ge1$, we give closed formulas for the local energies on tensor squares of the level-$l$ perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$, normalized to vanish at the all-zero coordinate tensors. The $D_4^{(3)}$ energy is the maximum of three defects, equivalently of nine linear forms in parameters of classical highest-weight elements. Eliminating these parameters yields the maximum of nine piecewise-linear functions of the twelve input coordinates. Tensor-compatible similarity identifies the $G_2^{(1)}$ energy at level $l$ with one third of the pullback of the $D_4^{(3)}$ energy at level $3l$, yielding the same coordinate formula. The formula has no explicit level dependence, respects natural coordinate-set inclusions between levels, and allows direct evaluation without the combinatorial $R$-matrix or crystal-graph traversal.

papers.title: Column rigidity in noncommutative $\L^1$-spaces and completely isometric embeddings of Hilbertian operator spaces
papers.abstract: We study exact embedding obstructions for Hilbertian operator spaces in noncommutative $\mathrm{L}^1$-spaces. We prove a quantitative version of the column inequality, whose equality case forces the absolute values of the entries to be proportional. We deduce that an operator space embedded completely isometrically in a noncommutative $\mathrm{L}^1$-space is a row Hilbert space whenever its first-column norms at the two-by-two level are Hilbert-Schmidt norms. This gives an exact embedding criterion for sums of weighted row and column spaces, including coordinate-dependent weights which are ordered in the same direction. In particular, $\mathrm{R}_n+\mathrm{C}_n$ does not embed completely isometrically into any noncommutative $\mathrm{L}^1$-space when $n \geq 2$. For $\mathrm{OH}_n$, whose complete isometric embeddability is established in a companion paper, we retain the common-support and commutative-target obstructions. We also show that distortion one is approached by matrix models but is attained by none of them, and that the matrix size must tend to infinity as the distortion tends to one.

papers.title: Complements of discriminants of real singularities of type $X_{10}$
papers.abstract:
Conjecturally complete lists of connected components of the complements of the discriminant varieties (aka wave fronts) of smooth function singularities of types $X_{10}^3$ and $X_{10}^1$ are provided. The combinatorial invariants of these components are defined and calculated.
  It is shown that the one-dimensional homology group of the complement of the discriminant of any versal deformation of any singularity of class $X_{10}^1$ contains a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^3$.

papers.title: Concurrent Strategies as Street Fibrations
papers.abstract:
Concurrent games and strategies based on event structures are an established and expressive model of interactive computation. In this paper we revisit the problem of equipping this model with symmetry. Symmetry is essential for many applications, but it is also a source of mathematical complexity, not least because strategies with symmetry can be compared up to several distinct notions of equivalence.
  Our first contribution is a complete characterization of two classes of strategies for which composition admits an identity. For these two classes the identity laws hold, respectively, up to a "weak" and a "strong" notion of equivalence. The main result is that the weak class of strategies corresponds precisely to those inducing Street fibrations over the game. We also show how the established "thin" approach to symmetry also fits in this general framework.
  A second contribution is a formal connection between games and setoid-valued profunctors. This follows a long tradition of relating games and relational models, but here additionally includes a very general model of symmetries. Our characterization of strategies as Street fibrations makes the connection to profunctors significantly easier to establish.

papers.title: Conifold Gap for the Quintic Threefold
papers.abstract:
We prove the all-genus conifold gap conjecture for the Gromov--Witten (GW) theories of the quintic threefold, other smooth Fermat Calabi--Yau threefold hypersurfaces, and local $\mathbb P^2$, as well as for the FJRW theories associated with these hypersurfaces.
  Our proof uses Mixed Spin P-field (MSP) theory and analogous master-space constructions. The central object is the \emph{cone-vertex theory}. We express this theory as a translation of the point CohFT via a formal Laplace transform and prove a universal conifold gap theorem for the resulting translated theories. The master-space construction then transfers the gap from the cone-vertex theory to the GW and FJRW theories.

papers.title: Construction of stability conditions on some Kuznetsov components
papers.abstract: We construct Bridgeland stability conditions on the Kuznetsov components of smooth Fano hypersurfaces of degrees three, four, and six and dimension at least three, smooth quartic double fivefolds, and smooth Fano complete intersections of three quadrics. For odd-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces and quartic double fivefolds, every connected component of the numerical stability manifold is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C\times\mathbb H$. For general cubic sevenfolds and quartic double fivefolds, spherical twists produce infinitely many distinct connected components.

papers.title: Constructions of contractibility in finite subset spaces
papers.abstract: The space of all finite non-empty subsets of a topological space $X$, also known as the Ran space of $X$, is weakly contractible for $X$ path connected. We consider subspaces $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ of the Ran space given by all subsets of $X$ of size at most $n$, and their first homotopy groups. These groups are known to be trivial for $n\geqslant 3$, though the proofs are not constructive. We draw an explicit contraction in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 3}(S^1)$ of the generator of $\pi_1(S^1)$, which we then use to conclude that the induced maps $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to \pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant 2n+1}(X))$ and $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)) \to \pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n+2}(X))$ are trivial for all positive integers $n$. Pathological maps with infinitely many strata changes in $\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X)$ are resolved via locally contractible neighbourhoods and exit paths. From this we conclude the triviality of $\pi_1(\mathrm{Ran}_{\leqslant n}(X))$, for all $n\geqslant 3$.

papers.title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
papers.abstract: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,\alpha,\beta,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{\lambda_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $\alpha/N$ and $\beta/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}\chi_\lambda(x)\,\Delta^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^\beta (x_a-p)^\alpha\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
papers.abstract: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.

papers.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.

papers.title: DEEP LOCI OF DOUBLE BOTT–SAMELSON VARIETIES
papers.abstract: We prove that the deep locus of a complex double Bott–Samelson variety associated with a positive braid is its stabilizer locus. Consequently, the deep locus is empty if and only if any two components of the braid closure are unlinked. This resolves Conjecture 4.45 of Castronovo, Gorsky, Simental, and Speyer.

papers.title: Derived graded modules
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the $\infty$-category of (complete) derived $G$-graded modules over a $G$-graded ring $R$ for a torsion-free abelian group $G$, and we study its foundational properties. Moreover, we prove a categorical equivalence between (complete) derived $G$-graded modules over $R$ and derived (formal) comodules over a certain comonad constructed from the group ring $R[G]$ of $G$ over $R$.

papers.title: Derived Torelli for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between the integral Mukai lattices of the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds is induced by an exact equivalence. The proof uses Markman--Mehrotra's comonad reconstruction method to recover both Kuznetsov components from a common Fourier--Mukai comonad on a moduli space of stable objects. As an application, we prove that the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds are equivalent whenever their Fano varieties of lines are derived equivalent.

papers.title: Distortion of Random Max Filters over Reflection Groups
papers.abstract:
A max filter with Gaussian templates $a_1,\dots,a_D$ is a
  $G$-invariant map $\R^d\to\R^D$, where $G$ is a finite reflection group. As
  $D\to\infty$ its distortion converges a.s to the condition number of
  $M_G^{1/2}$, where $M_G$ is the second-moment matrix of a standard Gaussian
  vector moved into a fundamental chamber of $G$. We compute this limit exactly
  for the sign and dihedral groups, and show it grows as $\Theta(\sqrt d)$,
  $\Theta(d^{3/2})$ and $\Theta(k)$ for the sign, symmetric and dihedral groups of order $2k$. The
  symmetric case bound uses a lower bound on the covariance of order
  statistics. For any finite $G$ we also show that the infimum defining the optimal lower Lipschitz
  constant of a piecewise-linear $G$-invariant map is a minimum.

papers.title: Equivariant Cleft Extensions and Singular Equivalences
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant lifting of cleft extensions of abelian categories and its impact on singularity categories. Specifically, we establish the necessary framework for lifting a cleft extension to a G-equivariant cleft extension. Furthermore, we prove that a restriction functor associated to a cleft extension induces a singular equivalence if and only if its equivariant counterpart does. As a concrete application, we demonstrate that the skew group ring of a $G$-equivariant $\theta$-extension is isomorphic to a $\widehat{\theta}$-extension of the base skew group ring, allowing us to lift singular equivalences for these structures.

papers.title: Exact diameter of the symmetric group with LX generators
papers.abstract: We prove an exact formula for the diameter of the directed Cayley graph for the symmetric group $S_n$ with generators $L$ (left cyclic shift) and $X$ (exchange of the first two elements). For every $n \geq 5$, we show that the diameter equals $(3n^2-8n+12)/4$ for even $n$ and $(3n^2-8n+9)/4$ for odd $n$. This resolves a longstanding question first proposed in the 1960's and refined in more recent work. The proof is AI-assisted and is based on a variety of combinatorial arguments. We also describe the agentic system we developed that led to this proof and looks highly promising for attacking other questions of this type. An accompanying Lean 4 formalization rigorously verifies the result.

papers.title: Extending Goldberg's Exact Sequence to Braid Groups of Graphs and Simplicial Complexes
papers.abstract: For a finite connected simplicial complex $X$, the strand map $\iota_\ast$, from $\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ to $\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_1(X,x_i^0)$, sends a pure braid to the homotopy classes of its strands. A theorem of Goldberg (1973) computes its kernel when $X$ is a closed surface other than $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$: the kernel is the normal closure of the pure braids supported in an embedded disc. We extend this picture to arbitrary finite connected simplicial complexes. Call $X$ $\textit{weakly Goldberg}$ if some contractible subcomplex $X_0\subseteq X$ realises Goldberg's description, $\ker\iota_\ast=\left\langle \operatorname{im}(\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)) \right\rangle$, and $\textit{Goldberg}$ if $X_0$ can moreover be chosen so that $\mathbb{P}_n(X_0)\to\mathbb{P}_n(X)$ is injective. We prove that the strand map is surjective if and only if $X\not\cong S^1$; that $X$ is weakly Goldberg if and only if its free part is a forest; and that $X$ is Goldberg if and only if it admits an $\textit{admissible tree}$ -- a maximal tree of a scaffold, compatible with the boundary and interior types of the attachments of the free part to the thick components. We also classify the complexes for which the kernel is trivial, settle the exceptional surfaces $S^2$ and $\mathbb{RP}^2$, and obtain complete answers for manifolds and for graphs. The main tools are a graph-of-spaces decomposition of the configuration space at a point of $X$ and a resolution procedure reducing an arbitrary complex to a simple model.

papers.title: Extensions at Nonzero p-Characters for Cartan-Type Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: For restricted simple Cartan-type Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge5$, the reduced enveloping algebra at every nonzero $p$-character is a matrix algebra over a terminal symmetric corner, and this corner determines the extensions. Central-socle traces recover its radical and its simple factors, and the first radical layer determines the degree-one extensions. For the Witt algebra $W(1;1)$, at even height $2\le h\le p-3$, the unique simple module has self-extension dimension $\min\{p-h-2,h+2\}$. At height two in characteristic seven, we present the Yoneda algebra as an eight-dimensional symmetric algebra tensored with a polynomial algebra on three central degree-two classes. An equivariant Tate resolution and cocycle identities prove the presentation in all degrees.

papers.title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursions for Higher Weil-Petersson Volumes on Moduli Spaces of Super Riemann Surfaces
papers.abstract: We derive an Eynard-Orantin topological recursion for intersection numbers involving Norbury's $\Theta$-class together with $\psi$-classes and higher $\kappa$-classes. These intersection numbers encode higher Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of super Riemann surfaces. The resulting recursion is a higher-$\kappa$ deformation of the topological recursion associated with the Bessel curve, which encodes the Br\'ezin-Gross-Witten model.

papers.title: Final coalgebras over R-modules
papers.abstract: Final coalgebras and the coinduction principle for coalgebras over $R$-modules, where $R$ is a commutative ring, are essential in determining the denotational behaviour of various types of linear weighted automata. The goal of this paper is to provide lower and upper bounds on the ordinals that are needed to construct final coalgebras over $R$-modules as the limit of a transfinite sequence of functor iterations. We give an example of a binary intersection preserving finitary functor on the category of abelian groups, which is the category of modules over integers, that fails to converge in $\omega \cdot 2$ steps, thus settling an open problem of Ad\'{a}mek, Milius, and Moss. Then we relate this to the failure of the Artinian property of the integers and show that all finitary functors on $R$-modules for a Noetherian ring $R$ with Krull dimension $n$, which preserve countable directed intersections and a generalised notion of monomorphism, converge in $\omega \cdot (n + 2)$ steps. We also establish how the connection between Aczel-Mendler bisimulation and behavioural equivalence is mediated by the functor $\operatorname{Ext}^1$. These results show that homological algebra tools can play an important role in coalgebra.

papers.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
papers.abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.

papers.title: Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations
papers.abstract: We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.

papers.title: Galois Actions on Energy-Harmonic Functions
papers.abstract: We study the action of $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on the solutions to the discrete Dirichlet problem for a graph with fixed edge energies. We establish transitivity of the Galois action outside a thin set in the parameter space and demonstrate that the exceptional thin set may be Zariski dense, so the conclusion cannot in general be replaced by one that holds on a Zariski-open set. Identifying the parameter locus where the Galois action is transitive constrains the possibilities for linking combinatorial and arithmetic properties of the discrete energy-harmonic Laplace equations and other systems of the same form.

papers.title: Generalized Howe curves of genus 4, 5, and 6 with completely decomposable Jacobians
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves are important objects in number theory and algebraic geometry, and the existence of such a curve of genus $g \geq 4$ is an open problem, for general characteristics $p > 0$. As a computational approach to this problem, Kudo-Harashita-Howe (2020) showed that a superspecial curve of genus 4 exists in each characteristic $p$ with $7 < p < 20000$. Their method restricted attention to a specific class of curves, known as Howe curves, for which superspeciality is reduced to those of curves of genus at most 2. In this paper, we focus on a more specific class of curves, namely Howe curves whose Jacobians decompose into a product of four elliptic curves. By restricting our attention to such curves, the superspeciality reduces to the supersingularity of elliptic curves, which enables us to construct a superspecial curve of genus 4 more efficiently than Kudo-Harashita-Howe's method. As our first main result, we confirmed by computer the existence of such superspecial curves of genus 4 in characteristics $p$ with $20000 < p < 10^6$. Using a similar approach, we also propose constructions of superspecial curves of genera 5 and 6 from only supersingular elliptic curves. Furthermore, computational experiments establish the existence of superspecial curves of genus 5 (resp. genus 6) in characteristics $p$ with $13 < p < 10^5$ (resp. $7 < p < 10^5$).

papers.title: Generalized parabolic Demazure modules and the N!/2-conjecture for two-row diagrams
papers.abstract: We study a family of generalized parabolic Demazure modules, i.e. of gl[x]-submodules of tensor products of integrable representations of the affine Lie algebra generated by tensor products of extremal vectors, and describe these modules by generators and relations. Realizing the Garsia--Haiman modules of two-row diagrams as fusion products of two local Weyl modules, we show that their y-graded components admit filtrations whose associated graded modules are isomorphic to tensor products of these generalized parabolic Demazure modules with the cohomology rings of Grassmannians. As a consequence, the Garsia-Haiman modules of two-row diagrams of a fixed size generate a distributive lattice, and the N!/2-conjecture holds for two-row diagrams.

papers.title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
papers.abstract: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. As an application of this geometrization, we prove Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets over p-adic fields: for quasisplit classical groups and their pure inner forms, all local Arthur packets are ABV-packets, and the distributions attached to these ABV-packets of Arthur type satisfy Arthur's local conjectures on twisted endoscopic character relations. This demonstrates the following general principle: for any reductive group G over a local field, an Arthur packet should be defined as an ABV-packet of Arthur type, equipped with the endoscopic pairing calculated by traces of actions on vanishing cycles or microlocalizations.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
papers.abstract: We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.

papers.title: GW/PT-correspondence for CY $4$-fold-II: Virtual Classes
papers.abstract:
Let $B$ be a complex manifold and $f:\bX\to B$ a derived \textit{complex-analytic} (not necessarily \textit{algebraic}) space with an oriented relative $(-2)$-shifted symplectic structure.
  We suppose that the closed symplectic form is locally exact in the completed relative de Rham complex, and construct a derived smooth manifold over $B$, independent of additional choices. When $f$ is proper and oriented, this gives integral virtual fundamental classes on its fibres.
  Our argument is heavily based on the strategy of Borisov-Joyce who already solved the \textit{algebraic} version of this problem, and uses \textit{derived differential geometry}. The proof also contains a relative analytic Darboux theorem a-la Brav-Bussi-Joyce, and has a natural analogue in Borel-Moore homology.
  We provide applications to complex-analytic enumerative geometry: in particular, to counting Pandharipande-Thomas pairs on compact and non-compact complex-analytic Calabi-Yau $4$-folds.
  This is part of a joint project with Felix Thimm dedicated to the proof of the GW/PT-correspondence for Calabi-Yau $4$-folds by implementing Pardon's programme in dimension $4$.

papers.title: Haagerup symmetries of the $E_8$ theory and conformal nets at central charge eight
papers.abstract: A Haagerup algebra is a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight with $\Rep(U)$ braided equivalent to the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category. Such an algebra has been proposed by Jiao, with a computer-assisted proof, and announced by Riesen and by Huang. We show that $U$ has exactly three holomorphic extensions, each isomorphic to $V_{E_8}$, and that the categories of modules over the corresponding Lagrangian algebras are the three Haagerup fusion categories of Grossman and Snyder. The extensions attached to $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ are the two lattice extensions of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$. Along a strategy outlined by Huang, we prove a recognition theorem for $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ among unitary fusion categories of rank six with three invertible objects, a noncommutative fusion ring and a pointed part with trivial associator. For regular unitary vertex operator algebras with Tener's bounded localized vertex operators, we prove that the fusion product of two unitary modules is unitarizable when one of them integrates to the conformal net. The explicit unitary algebra $S \subset V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ of our previous work, isomorphic to Jiao's algebra, is strongly local. Granting that Jiao's algebra is a Haagerup algebra, we deduce that the conformal net $\cal A_S$ is completely rational with $\Rep(\cal A_S) \cong Z(\cal H_3)$, that the Haagerup subfactor arises from $\cal A_S$, and that $\cal A_S$ solves a problem of Bischoff on generalized orbifolds. Under the same hypothesis, using a unitary structure on $V_{E_8 \oplus E_8}$ found by exact computer calculations, we prove that $S$ is completely unitary and that $\mathrm{Rep}(\cal A_S) \cong \mathrm{Rep}(S)$ through the correspondence given by smeared vertex operators. The diagonal construction and the passage to the twin algebra also show that every Haagerup algebra is completely unitary and satisfies Condition I+.

papers.title: Hammock coordinates for silting subcategories of derived-discrete algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce hammock coordinates to study the combinatorial structure of partial silting configurations in the bounded derived category of a derived-discrete algebra $\Lambda(r,n,m)$. By extracting exact integer inequalities from the Bobi\'nski--Gei\ss{}--Skowro\'nski Hom-hammock formula, we establish a closed-form criterion for pairwise partial silting both within any $\mathcal Z$-component and across distinct components. Using this coordinate framework, we establish three primary results. First, we prove the universal upper bound $|S| \le n+m$ on the cardinality of any partial silting configuration $S$ of $\mathcal Z$-objects ---both globally via Bongartz completion in the silting-discrete setting, and combinatorially within a single component via a $\Sigma^r$-invariant staircase argument. Second, we prove that this bound is universally sharp by constructing an explicit L-shaped partial silting configuration of size $n+m$ for every $\Lambda(r,n,m)$, alongside specialized diagonal configurations. Third, we show that the configuration lattice carries a faithful action of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z/g$ where $g = \gcd(r+m, n-r)$. We conclude by showing a structural obstruction to local determination: pairwise partial silting of consecutive objects in the lattice ordering does not imply global partial silting, due to the strict additivity of a coordinate defect along chains.

papers.title: Hecke eigenvalues in level 1 modulo powers of 2 and 3: Hatada's question (1981) and the Coleman-Stein conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a normalized Hecke eigenform of level $1$ and weight $k$, with eigenvalues $a_n(f)$. In 1981 Hatada asked whether $a_p(f)\equiv 1+p \pmod{2^a}$ whenever $p\equiv\pm1\pmod{2^{a-1}}$ and $6\le a\le 13$. Rustom's congruence modulo $128$ answers this for $a\le 7$. We show that the answer is affirmative for $a\le 10$ and negative for $a=11$, $12$ and $13$, the counterexamples coming from weight $16$ and $p=12289$. The proof combines Rustom's theorem with a certificate for $T_5$ modulo $512$ on period polynomials, a $2$-adic Galois law (for instance $a_p\equiv 1+p^{k-1}\pmod{2^{10}}$ for every $p\equiv 1\pmod 8$), and a reduction to a computation in a finite group. As a consequence, $a_p(f)=0$ implies $p\equiv -1\pmod{2^{11}}$.
