At the prime $3$ we show that, on Hatada's lattice of period polynomials, $T_2^2\equiv 9(k-1)^2\pmod{27}$, with refinements modulo $81$. This gives an independent proof of Conjecture 9.1 of Rustom without any ramification hypothesis and of the level $1$ case of the Coleman--Stein conjecture, both of which also follow from Rustom's recent classification modulo $81$. We also prove that $a_n(f)\equiv\sigma_{k-1}(n)\pmod{81}$ for every $n\equiv 1\pmod 3$, and a $3$-adic Galois law modulo $243$ on the Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, which gives congruences modulo $243$ and $729$ for suitable split primes and a bilinear law for primes $\ell\equiv 2\pmod 3$. Beyond $729$, for every prime $\ell\equiv 2\pmod 3$ we prove $a_\ell^2\equiv\sigma_{k-1}(\ell)^2\pmod{3^{\min(2j+2,10)}}$, where $j=v_3(\ell+1)$; the exponent $2j+2$ is attained for $j\le 4$ and fails for $j=5$. Each statement is marked as proved, known, verified or open. The finite computations are certified by seven Python scripts, provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras via generalized hep-derivors
papers.abstract: Higher-order many-sorted categorial algebras are many-sorted algebras whose carriers are strict higher-order categories and whose operations are higher-order functors. They admit a homogeneous and a heterogeneous presentation, both by partial algebras whose operation domains are given by existence equations. To relate these presentations and their dimensions, we introduce generalized hep-derivors between hierarchical equationally partial signatures. A generalized hep-derivor selects carriers by existence equations in one variable and interprets operation symbols by terms, with operation domains evaluated recursively in the transformed algebra. Every generalized hep-derivor induces a functor between categories of many-sorted partial algebras. The values of this functor satisfy the domain conditions wherever their operations are defined, and we characterize when the operations are defined exactly where these conditions hold. The functor induced by a composite receives a natural inclusion from the composite of the induced functors; this inclusion, which can be strict, makes the induced functors a normal lax indexed category. In finite dimensions, generalized hep-derivors realize graduation and unification as an equivalence between the homogeneous and heterogeneous presentations, and discretization as a left adjoint to truncation. In dimension $\omega$, we reconstruct the categories of $\omega$-categorial algebras as projective limits of their finite-dimensional truncations and obtain unification by a quotient construction; we also establish algebraic squares and compatibility with change of signature. Finally, for nonempty sets of sorts, we show that the finite-dimension condition in the homogeneous $\omega$-presentation is not axiomatizable by quasi-existence equations on its fixed signature.

papers.title: Hilton’s conjecture on cycle multiplicities
papers.abstract: We prove Hilton’s conjecture on the number of cycles of each length in dense Hamiltonian graphs. This resolves the problem posed by A. J.W. Hilton and recorded by Sheehan in 1977.

papers.title: Hodge theory and topology of Bogomolov--Guan manifolds
papers.abstract: Bogomolov--Guan manifolds are simply connected, irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds that are not K\"ahler, yet they echo hyperk\"ahler geometry in striking ways. We show that their Fr\"olicher spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ and that their Hodge numbers are stable under small deformations. The general fibers of their natural Lagrangian fibration are rationally null-homologous, and the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki form is degenerate. Despite this, in every dimension, the Euler characteristics agree with those of generalized Kummer manifolds. In dimensions four and six, we compute the full Hodge diamonds and all Chern and Pontryagin numbers. Surprisingly, these characteristic numbers are the same as the generalized Kummer ones, even though the Betti numbers differ and the Hodge diamonds are asymmetric.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

papers.title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
papers.abstract: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.

papers.title: iCanonical basis arising from quasi-split rank one iquantum group
papers.abstract: We compute icanonical basis of the quasi-split rank one modified iquantum group, by obtaining explicit transition matrices among the icanonical basis, monomial basis, and standardized canonical basis; all these bases can be naturally categorified. These transition matrices follow from their counterparts computed in this paper among the icanonical basis, monomial basis, and canonical basis on simple finite-dimensional modules of quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$.

papers.title: Idempotent Ultrafilters and Closed Images of Complete Semilattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every continuous homomorphism from a complete topologized semilattice to a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice has closed image, answering a question of Banakh and Bardyla. The main step is the convergence of idempotent ultrafilters on complete semitopological semilattices. We also prove that, for every complete subsemilattice $X$ of a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $Y$, the natural order of $X$ is closed in $Y\times Y$. In particular, the natural order of every complete Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $X$ is closed in $X\times X$.

papers.title: Igusa Stacks and the Cohomology of Shimura Varieties
papers.abstract: We construct functorial Igusa stacks for all Hodge-type Shimura varieties, proving a conjecture of Scholze and extending earlier results of the fourth-named author for PEL-type Shimura varieties. Using the Igusa stack, we construct a sheaf on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ that controls the cohomology of the corresponding Shimura variety. We use this sheaf and the spectral action of Fargues-Scholze to prove a compatibility between the cohomology of Shimura varieties of Hodge type and the semisimple local Langlands correspondence of Fargues-Scholze, generalizing the Eichler-Shimura relation of Blasius-Rogawski to arbitrary level at $p$. When the given Shimura variety is proper, we show moreover that the sheaf is perverse, which allows us to prove new torsion vanishing results for the cohomology of Shimura varieties.

papers.title: Intersection theory on derived stacks
papers.abstract: We define integral cycle complexes and Chow homology of derived Artin stacks. To any quasi-smooth family of derived Artin stacks we associate a bivariant fundamental class, encoding the virtual fundamental classes of its fibres and their deformation invariance up to coherent homotopy. We extend the Riemann-Roch theorem of Baum-Fulton-MacPherson from quasi-projective schemes to derived Artin stacks, and thereby obtain a virtual Riemann-Roch formula for quasi-smooth derived Artin stacks. As another application of the formalism, we construct intersection products on regular Artin stacks locally of finite type over a field. Finally, we prove an integral comparison of our Chow homology with the cycle-theoretic Chow groups of Kresch.

papers.title: Interval Replacements of Persistence Modules
papers.abstract: Persistence modules indexed by finite posets arise in topological data analysis. Unlike in the one-parameter case, they need not decompose into interval modules. Interval replacements approximate them by formal differences of interval decomposable modules. Extending earlier work on 2D-grids, we study these replacements for arbitrary compression systems. Different choices can give different interval rank invariants and replacements, including those related to interval resolutions on commutative ladders. Our main results are an explicit formula for interval ranks and an essential-cover theorem. Using Auslander--Reiten theory, we express interval ranks in terms of ranks of matrices formed from the structure maps of the module. The essential-cover theorem recovers each interval rank from a suitable restriction of the module. The replacement construction preserves the corresponding interval rank invariant, which recovers the usual rank invariant on segments. Essential covers also give a sufficient condition for two compression systems to yield the same invariant. For total compression, the invariant coincides with the generalized rank invariant of Kim and M\'emoli. On 2D-grids, essential covers recover the zigzag formula of Dey, Kim, and M\'emoli for this invariant.

papers.title: Invariant Shape Analysis of Surfaces with Spherical Topology
papers.abstract: Every real spherical harmonic of even degree is congruent to its mirror image. We prove that a real spherical harmonic of odd degree $n\ge3$ with distinct Maxwell axes is congruent to its mirror image if and only if the hyperelliptic curve of genus $n-1$ defined by its binary form has a reduced automorphism of even order whose lift acts on the form by $-1$. We then determine the locus of these curves: it is the locus of curves with an extra involution if and only if $n-1$ is a power of two, and otherwise it also contains, for each even divisor $k$ of $n-1$ with odd cofactor $d\ge3$, an irreducible family $y^2=x K(x^{2k})$, $\deg K=d$, with generic reduced automorphism group $\Z/2k$. For $n=3$ the condition is the vanishing of the skew invariant of the binary sextic. As an application, the invariants of the truncated spherical harmonic expansion of a genus-zero surface, in a conformal parameterization normalized by its conformal barycenter, give a descriptor that is exactly invariant under parameterization, position and scale, records handedness, and is stable in the orbit distance.

papers.title: Isogeny rigidity under algebraic group actions and finite translation orbits
papers.abstract: We study finite orbits generated by fibrewise translations on varieties carrying two abelian fibrations. Under natural dominance and generation hypotheses, non-isotriviality of the first family forces points with finite orbit to lie over proper closed subsets of both bases. This extends results of Corvaja, Tsimerman and Zannier to complex families of arbitrary, possibly different relative dimensions, including torsors. The proof combines relative Manin-Mumford with a general isogeny rigidity theorem for algebraic group actions.

papers.title: Isomorphism classes and geometric classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras and the length function
papers.abstract: We investigate the algebraic classification of Jordan algebras of dimensions at most three over arbitrary fields with more than two elements. Our approach combines the theory of nilalgebras and radicals with Peirce, Wedderburn decompositions and the length function. In characteristic two, we adapt the Peirce decomposition to organize the classification, including the field-dependent isomorphism conditions among parametrized families. We also study the varieties of Jordan algebra structures up to dimension three over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Besides explicit degenerations and standard arguments, we introduce the alicyclic and characteristic conditions as geometric obstructions to degeneration. We determine the rigid algebras and irreducible components in both dimensions. In dimension three, one component is the nine-dimensional affine space of square-zero products; unlike the other three components, it contains no open orbit.

papers.title: Iterating the Gupta–Ndiaye–Norin–Wei method: a computer-verified bound $R(k)\le 3.7698^{k+o(k)}$
papers.abstract: Gupta, Ndiaye, Norin and Wei (GNNW) recast the Campos–Griffiths–Morris–Sahasrabudhe method as an inductive theorem that turns a known bound on off-diagonal Ramsey numbers into a better one. With two applications they obtained $R(k)\le (3.7992\ldots)^{k+o(k)}$. They also reported an unverified, AI-suggested third application giving $3.78233\ldots$. We make three observations about their framework. (i) The free function $M$ can be optimised pointwise. (ii) For a fixed input, the best output exponent is the least solution of an explicit first-order differential inequality. (iii) GNNW's Theorem 14 needs only $F\in C^1$ with locally Lipschitz derivative. We then construct an explicit chain of eight applications and verify every hypothesis by interval arithmetic on the whole range $0<\lambda\le 1$, with a hand-proved estimate covering $\lambda\to0$. The verification was done twice, with independent code, libraries and enclosure strategies. This proves $R(k)\le 3.76973^{k+o(k)}$, and in particular confirms GNNW's $3.78233$. Numerically, iterating the optimal step converges to about $3.7690$, which suggests this is close to the limit of the GNNW method in its present form.

papers.title: Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent type
papers.abstract: We study the Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent types and its application to the representation theory of the (mixed, small, and Lusztig) quantum supergroups. Using local and global models and SW-Zastava spaces, we construct factorization functors and compare the Iwahori Gaiotto category with the category $O$ of the mixed quantum supergroup. We then study the images of intersection cohomology sheaves and the metaplectic Hecke action. In type A, we describe the finite and affine monodromic categories, the corresponding Yokonuma--Hecke actions, and their role in the Kazhdan--Lusztig algorithm. The last section treats the pointwise purity.

papers.title: Large N instantons, BPS states, and the replica limit
papers.abstract: We study the relation between large N instantons and conventional instantons, focusing on matrix models and topological strings. We show that the resurgent properties of the perturbative series at fixed but arbitrary N, including the replica limit N = 0, can be obtained from large N instantons. In the case of topological strings, it has been conjectured that the resurgent structure encoded by large N instantons is closely related to the spectrum of BPS states. We give direct evidence for this connection in the case of Seiberg-Witten theory and other topological string models, and we show in detail how the resurgent properties at fixed N follow from the large N theory, and therefore can be used to obtain information on BPS invariants.

papers.title: Linear independence of even Dirichlet beta values
papers.abstract: Let $\beta(s)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ denote the Dirichlet beta function. For all sufficiently large even integers $s$, we prove $\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{Q}}\{\beta(2),\beta(4),\ldots,\beta(s)\}\geq 0.21\sqrt{s/\log s}$.

papers.title: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<\rho<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloor\rho n\rfloor,n-\lfloor\rho n\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves. They are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes when $q$ is sufficiently large. An infinite subfamily has exact length $n=\sqrt q+2gq^{1/4}+1$.

papers.title: Minimal $a$-numbers of Artin--Schreier covers of ordinary curves
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $d$ be a positive integer not divisible by $p$. We define a non-empty Zariski open subset $U$ of the space of polynomials of degree $d$, and for $f(x)\in U(k)$, we compute the $a$-number of the curve defined by $y^p-y=f(x)$. This $a$-number realizes a lower bound given by Booher and Cais, so the latter is tight. Our result also implies that the bound of Booher and Cais for minimal $a$-numbers of Artin-Schreier covers of ordinary curves is tight.

papers.title: Modular Dvoretzky, Type-Cotype, Khinchin-Kahane and Grothendieck Inequality Problems
papers.abstract: We ask for noncommutative versions of following four: (1) Dvoretzky Theorem, (2) Type-Cotype Definition, (3) Khinchin-Kahane Inequalities, (4) Grothendieck Inequality.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of rank 2 sheaves on $\mathbb P^3$ via Quot schemes
papers.abstract: We study the Gieseker--Maruyama moduli space $M_{c_3}$ of stable rank 2 torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^3$ with Chern classes $c_1=-1$, $c_2=1$, and odd $c_3 \le 1$. Every such sheaf $E$ has reflexive hull $E^{\ast\ast}$ parametrised by $M_1$, and the quotient $E^{\ast\ast}/E$ is a 0-dimensional sheaf of length $n = (1-c_3)/2$. We prove that $M_{c_3}$ is isomorphic to the relative Quot scheme $\mathsf{Quot}_{\mathbb{P}^3 \times M_1/M_1}(\mathscr{R},n)$, where $\mathscr{R}$ is the universal reflexive sheaf over $M_1$. Our technique combines (i) Bridgeland-type wall-crossing in Donaldson--Thomas theory, (ii) the theory of good moduli spaces, (iii) deformation theory in dgla and Ext-quiver language. We deduce that $M_{c_3}$ is connected, and we analyse its \emph{smoothable component} $M_{c_3}^{\mathsf{main}}$, proving it is rational and generically smooth of dimension $4n+3$. We further prove that $\dim \mathrm{Sing} M_{c_3} \geq 4n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$. Finally, we provide a geometric characterisation for the cases $n\leq 2$. We show that $M_{-1}$ is a smooth rational projective variety of dimension 7 and compute its motive in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, while $M_{-3}$ is shown to be an integral, normal variety of dimension 11 that is regular in codimension 4.

papers.title: Monoidal categories graded by partial commutative monoids
papers.abstract: Effectful categories have two classes of morphisms: pure morphisms, which form a monoidal category; and effectful morphisms, which can only be combined monoidally with central morphisms (such as the pure ones), forming a premonoidal category. This suggests seeing morphisms of an effectful category as carrying a grade that combines under the monoidal product in a partially defined manner. We axiomatize this idea with the notion of monoidal category graded by a partial commutative monoid (PCM). Monoidal categories arise as the special case of grading by the singleton PCM, and effectful categories arise from grading by a two-element PCM. Further examples include grading by powerset PCMs, modelling non-interfering parallelism for programs accessing shared resources, and grading by intervals, modelling bounded resource usage. We show that effectful categories form a coreflective subcategory of PCM-graded monoidal categories; introduce cartesian structure, recovering Freyd categories; and describe PCM-graded monoidal categories as monoids by viewing a PCM as a thin promonoidal category.

papers.title: Multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair and its unitary analogue
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair associated with $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and its unitary similitude analogue associated with $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)\times\mathrm{GU}(1,1)(F)$. Both results hold for all irreducible admissible representations over non-Archimedean local fields of characteristic zero. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent reduces the proofs to the analysis of closed orbits and their normal representations. The unitary proof combines reductions to the linear case with a rational classification of closed orbits and a separate analysis of the remaining normal representations. We also establish multiplicity one for unitary Shalika periods of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ with arbitrary irreducible admissible coefficients. A theta-period identity relates these periods to the unitary spherical pair. By varying the splitting character, we prove that every irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ occurs as a quotient of a suitable big theta lift, allowing the multiplicity-one bound to pass to the Shalika periods. The linear argument also recovers Rallis's multiplicity-one theorem for twisted Jacquet modules of $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)$.

papers.title: Normality of closures of conormal bundles to Schubert cells for $\operatorname{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: We prove normality of closures of the conormal bundle to certain Schubert cells in the flag variety for $\operatorname{GL}_n$ coming from Grassmannians. Our argument uses a Zelevinsky-type resolution of singularities, and through a sequence of cohomological computations based on the Borel--Weil--Bott theorem, we reduce normality to a problem about Kronecker coefficients, which we solve by applying results of Knutson and Tao from honeycomb theory.

papers.title: Normalizers in the category of topological groups
papers.abstract: We show that the category of morphisms of topological groups admits split extension classifiers and hence the category of topological groups admits normalizers. We give explicit descriptions of both normalizers and of split extension classifiers of morphisms of topological groups in terms of split extension classifiers of topological groups.

papers.title: On Bounds for Reciprocal Sums and Residues in Collatz Orbits, and Their Consequences
papers.abstract: We prove uniform bounds for reciprocal sums and residue products along Collatz paths. Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite nonrepeating shortcut path whose input states are greater than $1$, let $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}$ be the sum of the reciprocals of its odd inputs, and let $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ be its finite-path residue. Then $\mathcal R_{\mathcal F}<1, \qquad \rho_{\mathcal F}<\frac{4}{3}. $ For the first-arrival trajectory of a terminating positive integer $n$, these inequalities give $\mathcal R(n)<1, \qquad \rho(n)=\frac{2^{E(n)}}{3^{O(n)}n}<\frac{4}{3},$ where $E(n)$ and $O(n)$ are the division and odd-operation counts. More generally, when each odd value greater than $1$ is counted once, the corresponding reciprocal-sum and residue bounds hold for every forward orbit, without a termination assumption. The proof combines verified finite height-delay records and residue bounds, canonical-block reciprocal estimates, and an exact finite count organized by gap brackets. Gap brackets, closely related to parity vectors, record the divisions by two between successive odd inputs and organize the finite counting argument; together with a related coordinate representation, they also yield exact formulas for reconstructing finite trajectories. After taking base-$2$ logarithms, the bound $\rho_{\mathcal F}<4/3$ leaves an uncertainty of less than $1/2$ in the relation between the even- and odd-operation counts. Since these counts are integers, either count is determined exactly by the other count and the path endpoints. We obtain nearest-integer restrictions on the changes in $E$ and $O$ between adjacent integers, apart from explicit small exceptions, and prove that adjacent terminating integers of equal height have identical operation counts. Thus every equal-height streak lies in a single operation-count class. We further introduce the charge $\lambda=E-2O$ and associated height and charge slice functions to study the persistence and eventual break of equal-height streaks. We distinguish class records, which are the least starting integers attaining specified values, from delay records, which attain new extrema relative to all smaller starting integers. The resulting record theory shows that $\lambda$-delay records form a subsequence of the odd-count delay records, which form a subsequence of the common division-count and height-delay list. On the class side, the nonpositive charge-class records lie among the odd-count class records, which lie among the division-count class records, which in turn lie among the height-class records. The corresponding hierarchies also hold for first-arrival paths to a common endpoint $z$ when $z=1$ or when $z>2$ is nonperiodic under the shortcut map.

papers.title: On F-pure thresholds and quasi-F-purity of hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We show that quasi-$F$-pure but not $F$-pure isolated quasi-homogeneous hypersurface singularities necessarily have $F$-pure threshold $1 - \frac{1}{p}$. This extends work of Bhatt and Singh beyond the Calabi-Yau case. We also classify the (quasi)-$F$-purity of Fermat hypersurfaces.

papers.title: On Fujita's conjecture for a general hyperk\"ahler manifold in the standard series of examples
papers.abstract: For the moduli spaces $\mathcal{V}(K3)_{d,t}^n$ and $\mathcal{V}(\text{Kum})_{d,t}^n$ of polarized hyperk\"ahler manifolds of $\text{Hilb}^n(K3)$-type and $\text{Kum}^n$-type respectively, with polarization with square $2d$ and divisibility $t$, we study general base point freeness and very ampleness of the polarization. We provide conditions, in terms of $n, d, t$ that guarantee that the general polarization, in any connected component of these moduli spaces, to be base point free or very ample.

papers.title: On motivic multiplicativity of cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective complex variety of dimension $n$ with trivial Chow groups, and let $f: X\rightarrow Y$ be a cyclic cover of degree $d$ branched over a smooth ample divisor $D\in |dL|$. We show that a naturally constructed Chow--K\"unneth decomposition of $X$ is $m$-fold $mn$-multiplicative for each integer $m\geq2$ and that its stable motivic multiplicativity defect satisfies $\mathfrak{sd}(X)\leq 2dn$. If, in addition, each positive-codimension cycle class on $Y$ is supported on $D$, then a double cover admits motivic $0$-multiplicativity. As a further application, we show that any smooth Gushel--Mukai sixfold admits motivic 0-multiplicativity. Moreover, we establish the sharp modified-diagonal property for all smooth double EPW sextics, confirming a conjecture of O'Grady for these varieties.

papers.title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperk\"ahler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.

papers.title: On Riemannian Geometry in Elastic Diffeology
papers.abstract: Blohmann's tangent functor makes the category of elastic diffeological spaces a Cartesian tangent category in the sense of Cockett and Cruttwell. We use this structure to develop Riemannian geometry on elastic diffeological spaces. Following Cockett and Cruttwell, with additional axioms for scalar multiplication, we introduce connections, covariant derivatives and curvature; for a Riemannian metric we prove a Koszul formula and the uniqueness of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative. Our main result is a variational characterization of geodesics: if a full connection whose vertical part is Levi-Civita admits a geodesic flow fixing the zero section, then the critical paths of the energy functional are exactly the paths satisfying the geodesic equation, and regular length-minimizing paths are geodesics after constant-speed reparametrization. On elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, completeness of the geodesic spray yields such a flow and uniqueness of geodesics. The results apply to quotients of complete Riemannian manifolds by free isometric actions of countable groups, such as irrational tori, and, under a tangent-commuting hypothesis, to mapping spaces from a closed manifold into elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, including free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: On the largest irreducible factor of an odd perfect polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_2$
papers.abstract: A polynomial $A$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is perfect if it equals the sum $\sigma(A)$ of all its divisors, and odd if it is coprime to $x^2+x$. Canaday conjectured in 1941 that 1 is the only odd perfect polynomial. Known necessary conditions on a counterexample bound its number of distinct irreducible factors ($\omega\ge 5$, Gallardo and Rahavandrainy), its number of irreducible factors counted with multiplicity and its degree ($\Omega\ge 12$ and $\deg A>200$, Cengiz, Pollack and Trevino), and, when all exponents equal 2, the degree of its smallest irreducible factor (at least 40, Gallardo). We bound a different invariant: every odd perfect polynomial $A\ne 1$ has an irreducible factor of degree at least 20. The proof reduces the question, for each $D$, to a finite system: if all irreducible factors of $A$ have degree at most $D$, the exponents of $A$ belong to an explicit finite set, through the cyclotomic factorisation of $\sigma(P^h)$ and the multiplicative order of $P$ modulo the factors of $\sigma(P^h)$. An iterated sieve on the resulting production relations empties for every $D\le 19$. The computation was carried out twice, by two independent programs, with identical results; the second program is attached as an ancillary file. As a cross-check of the method, the same programs reproduce, by the orbit argument of Gallardo and Rahavandrainy, the exclusion of every prime of degree at most 30 as the smallest factor of a special perfect polynomial, in agreement with the published bounds.

papers.title: On the regularity index of the minimum distance function in projective nested Cartesian codes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a projective nested product of fields and let $\delta_X(d)$ be the minimum distance in degree $d\geq 1$ of the projective nested Cartesian code $C_X(d)$. The regularity index ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ of the minimum distance function $\delta_X$ is the minimum integer $d_0\geq 0$ such that $\delta_X(d)=1$ for $d\geq d_0$. We give a formula for ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ by determining an indicator function of least degree for each point of $X$ and using the fact that ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ is the ${\rm v}$-number of the vanishing ideal $I_X$ of $X$. Then we give an arithmetical criterion that characterizes when $X$ is Cayley--Bacharach.

papers.title: On uniform large genus asymptotics of Witten's intersection numbers
papers.abstract: Following ideas from [14], we give a uniform large genus asymptotics for primitive psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of stable algebraic curves, and extend this result including insertions of zeros in a certain uniform way. Application to a particular formal solution of the Painlev\'e I equation is given. We also use a method from [14] to give a new proof of the polynomiality conjecture on large genus asymptotic expansions of psi-class intersection numbers.

papers.title: Operator Fej\'{e}r--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
papers.abstract:
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space.
  In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds.
  Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fej\'er--Riesz theorem yields certificates.

papers.title: Orbit structures on real double flag varieties for the Siegel parabolic subgroups
papers.abstract:
Let $ G $ be a connected reductive algebraic group over $ \mathbb{R} $, and $ H $ its symmetric subgroup. For parabolic subgroups $ P_{G} \subset G $ and $ P_{H} \subset H $, the product of flag varieties $ \mathfrak{X} = H/P_H \times G/P_G $ is called a double flag variety, on which $ H $ acts diagonally.
  Now let $G$ be either $\mathrm{U}(n,n)$ or $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{R})$. We classify the $H$-orbits on $ \mathfrak{X} $ in both cases and show that they admit exactly the same parametrization. Concretely, each orbit corresponds to a signed partial involution, which can be encoded by simple combinatorial graphs. The orbit structure reduces to several families of smaller flag varieties, and we find an intimate relation of the orbit decomposition to Matsuki duality and Matsuki-Oshima's notion of clans.
  We also compute the Galois cohomology of each orbit, which exhibits another classification of the orbits by explicit matrix representatives.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Quantum Groups Revisited
papers.abstract: We present the RLL-realization of extended orthosymplectic quantum supergroups for any parity sequence, with R-matrices evaluated in the earlier work [Lett. Math. Phys. 116 (2026), 55, 97 pages, arXiv:2408.16720]. Our isomorphism is compatible with the internal structure of generalized doubles. We also relate different sign conventions through 2-cocycle twists.

papers.title: PARAMETER MONOTONICITY FOR GENERALIZED k-MARKOV NUMBERS
papers.abstract: We prove that the order reversal asked about in Question 35 of Banaian and Huang cannot occur for generalized k-Markov numbers, answering their question negatively.

papers.title: Partial character tables for $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-spetses
papers.abstract:
Let ${\mathbb{G}}$ be a simply connected ${\mathbb{Z}}_\ell$-spets, let $q$ be a prime power, prime to $\ell$ and let $S$ be the underlying Sylow $\ell$-subgroup. Firstly, motivated by known formulae for values of Deligne-Lusztig characters of finite reductive groups, we propose a formula for the values of the unipotent characters of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ on the elements of $S$. Using this, we explicitly list the unipotent character values of the ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-spets $G_{24}(q)$ related to the Benson-Solomon fusion system Sol$(q)$, and the Aguad\'{e} ${\mathbb{Z}}_5$-spets $G_{29}(q)$.
  Secondly, when $\ell > 2$ is a very good prime for ${\mathbb{G}}$, the Weyl group $W$ of ${\mathbb{G}}$ has order coprime with $\ell$, and $q\equiv1\pmod\ell$ we introduce a formula for the values of characters in the principal block of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ which extends the Curtis-Schewe type formulae for groups of Lie type, and which we show to satisfy a version of block orthogonality.
  In both cases we formulate and provide evidence for several conjectures concerning the proposed values.

papers.title: Partial Linearity: Diagolinear Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce and study diagolinear categories. These are pointed categories equipped with sum-like and product-like monoidal structures, where diagonal matrices of morphisms between two sequences of objects are (uniquely) realizable as morphisms from the sum of the first sequence to the product of the second sequence. We formulate and prove the coherence theorem for diagolinear categories and study the universal construction that realizes also the non-diagonal matrices (equivalently, turns the two monoidal structures into actual categorical sum and product). We also compare diagolinear categories with duoidal categories.

papers.title: Planar Convexity of Isotropy Orbits via Cohomology and Common Zeros
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a noncompact simple real Lie algebra with a Cartan decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{p}$. Let $K$ denote the connected Lie group corresponding to $\mathfrak{k}$. Then $K$ acts on $\mathfrak{p}$ via the adjoint representation. In this paper, we prove that for every $C\in\mathfrak{p}$ and every real linear map $L:\mathfrak{p}\to\mathbb{R}^2$, the linear image $L(K\cdot C)$ of the orbit $K\cdot C\subset\mathfrak{p}$ is convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$, except for the circle orbits when $\mathfrak{g}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ne0$. By the two-piece property of isotropy orbits, any point omitted from the interior of the convex hull of a planar projection induces a nonzero class in the first integral cohomology of the orbit. This class vanishes directly in the non-Hermitian case, whereas in the Hermitian case we show that it vanishes by using the central circle action and a common-zero theorem of Gichev for Laplace eigenfunctions. Our approach treats classical and exceptional noncompact simple real Lie algebras uniformly and extends to real semisimple Lie algebras via Minkowski sums.

papers.title: Pontryagin-Weiss classes and a rational decomposition of spaces of homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We construct a rational homotopy pullback decomposition for variants of the classifying space of the group of homeomorphisms for a large class of manifolds. This has various applications, including a rational section of the stabilisation map ${\rm Top}(d)\rightarrow {\rm Top}$ of the space of homeomorphisms of ${\bf R}^d$ for $d\ge 6$, or a new method to construct topological bundles and detect characteristic classes thereof. Some steps in the proofs may be of independent interest, such as the construction of a nullhomotopy of the twice-iterated stabilisation map for the space of orientation-preserving derived automorphisms of the rational $E_d$-operad, results on recovering boundaries of manifolds from their interior in the context of embedding calculus, or a treatment of tensor products of truncated $\infty$-operads.

papers.title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points for $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
papers.abstract: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output $\mathcal{H}_2$-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem. We prove, under suitable genericity assumptions, that their set of complex solutions is finite and that all solutions occur without multiplicity. Moreover, we derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders. Throughout, we provide a self-contained and application-oriented exposition of the algebro-geometric tools required for our analysis, with the aim of making them accessible to the broader engineering community.

papers.title: Positive integral points on Mordell-Schinzel surfaces
papers.abstract: We apply the theory of generalised cluster algebras to classify the finiteness of positive integral points on the class of log K3 surfaces defined by $xyz = G(x,y)$ where $G$ has positive coefficients. We furthermore establish results on Zariski density, number of orbits and asymptotic growth of such points. These provide a Diophantine realisation of the finite-affine-indefinite trichotomy of rank-two root systems.

papers.title: Powers of a Prime in the Image of Summatory Valuation Functions
papers.abstract: J.-L. Nicolas asked how often a power of $2$ belongs to the image of $c(n)=\sum_{k\le n}2^{v_2(k)}$, where $v_2$ is the $2$-adic valuation, and showed that both the number $A(x)$ of exponents $a\le x$ with $2^a$ in the image and the number $B(x)$ of the other exponents tend to infinity. We prove the identity $c(n)=n+\frac12\sum_{i}i\,2^{i}$, the sum running over the positions of the binary digits $1$ of $n$, so that $2^a$ lies in the image of $c$ if and only if $2^{a+3}$ is a sum of distinct terms of the superincreasing sequence $(j2^j)_{j\ge1}$. For every exponent there is at most one possible largest term $K$, given by $K+\lceil\log_2K\rceil=a+3$, and no such $K$ exists exactly when $a=2^r+r-2$. The remaining exponents are decided by an explicit recursion on pairs of integers bounded by $a+3$, in at most $a+1$ steps. We give the closed formula $c(2^{K-2}+2^{K-s-2})=2^{K+h-3}$ for $s=2^k$, $h\equiv k\pmod{2^{k+1}}$ and $K=(2^{h+s}+s)/(2^s+1)$, and infinite explicit families of exponents $a$ for which $2^a$ is not in the image, indexed by $s=3$ and $s=2^i$; the families given by Nicolas are the cases $s=1$ and $s=2$. As a consequence, $A(x)\ge(2+o(1))\log_2x$ and $B(x)\ge(\frac54+\frac12\sum_{i\ge1}\frac{1}{2^i-1}+o(1))\log_2x=(2.0533\ldots+o(1))\log_2x$. We prove that the states of the recursion form a forest, rooted at the states $(J,0)$ and at the failing states, in which every state $(J',w')$ has exactly $v_2(J'+1+w')$ children; that the sets $S_J$ of successful states are symmetric; that exactly half of them lie in the tree of the root $(1,0)$; that $N(2k+1)=N(2k)$; that $4\mid N(J)$ for $J\ge4$; and that $S_J$ satisfies a recursion from the smallest elements upwards, with period $J/2$ for even $J$. The symmetry gives further explicit families, among them $c(2^{2^r}-1)=2^{2^r+r-1}$, and the improved bounds $A(x)\ge(3.9655\ldots+o(1))\log_2x$ and $B(x)\ge(2.8178\ldots+o(1))\log_2x$. For every prime $p$, the function $c_p(n)=\sum_{k\le n}p^{v_p(k)}$ counts the factor $1-X$ in $(1-X)\cdots(1-X^n)$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$; we extend to it the reduction, the unique candidate, the recursions and the symmetry, give explicit families, and describe completely the exponents rejected at the first step, which occur only for odd $p$. We also report experiments in exact integer arithmetic: every statement is checked by three independent methods, the values of $A(x)$ reproduce the table of Nicolas, the sets $S_J$ are computed for $J\le131072$, and $A(x)/x$ lies between $0.5132$ and $0.8750$ for $x=1000,2000,\dots,131000$.

papers.title: Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms
papers.abstract: Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and gives a subexponential error. For arbitrary smooth plateau tests, the prime number theorem of Harcos and Thorner gives an error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log T, without a self-contragredience assumption. The stronger prime number theorem of Liu and Ye gives a subexponential remainder under its stated structural assumptions, with the possible norm-twist terms made explicit. To obtain arithmetic information beyond this overlap, we compute the correlation expansion at every fixed level and inverse-logarithmic order within the original strict small-support range. We treat the pair and higher correlations separately, using Jiang's rational-field fixed-data estimates to justify the required prime-power convergence. The pair calculation identifies the mixed arithmetic finite parts and gives detailed error estimates, including the contribution of norm twists. The higher-level calculation retains connected prime-power invariants, whose first cubic contribution appears at order (log T)^{-3}. Explicit third- and fourth-level formulas and examples explain the arithmetic content of these coefficients and the limitations of self-correlations. Varying powers of the probe separates their mixed components. These formulas, together with the distinct-index sieve, provide a collection of arithmetic probe responses toward the further problem of recovering automorphic induction structure.

papers.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
papers.abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).

papers.title: Quasi-$F^e$-splittings and quasi-$F$-regularity
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of quasi-$F^e$-splittings, quasi-$F$-regularity, and quasi-$+$-regularity.

papers.title: Quasi-polynomial valuations of lattice polytopes
papers.abstract: We prove that for any valuation $\varphi$ of lattice polytopes in ${\mathbb R}^m$, which is quasi-polynomial with respect to ${\mathbb Z}^m$-translations, and any lattice polytope $P$, the function $\varphi(nP)$ is quasi-polynomial in $n$.

papers.title: Quasitoposes as elementary quotient completions
papers.abstract: We characterise when the elementary quotient completion of an elementary doctrine, introduced in previous work by the first and third authors, is a quasitopos. Since the elementary quotient completion generalises the notion of exact completion of a cartesian category with weak equalisers to the setting of elementary doctrines, as proposed by F.W. Lawvere, the characterisation established in this paper, generalises previous results on exact completions, which include A. Carboni and E. Vitale's characterisation in terms of projective objects, Carboni and G. Rosolini's characterisation of locally cartesian closed exact completions, as revised by J. Emmenegger, and M. Menni's characterisation of exact completions that are toposes.

papers.title: RaFH and CRaFH superalgebras: Frobenius forms, representation theory and respectability
papers.abstract:
We introduce \emph{RaFH superalgebras}, which are Rees affine Frobenius Hecke superalgebras. These algebras are defined by generators and relations, using \emph{Frobenius-tensor superalgebras} to axiomatise tensor powers of Frobenius superalgebras together with their copairing elements. The RaFH superalgebras include, as special cases, the affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of type $A$, the affine Sergeev superalgebras, the affine wreath product algebras and quantum affine wreath algebras, as well as the recently introduced quantum wreath product algebras in the special case of the superflip braiding. We study the RaFH superalgebras from both structural and representation theoretic points of view. We prove a basis theorem for the RaFH superalgebras, construct universal Jucys--Murphy elements, and classify their simple modules over an algebraically closed field via atomic superalgebras, which are smaller RaFH superalgebras of Hecke, Clifford or wreath type.
  We then study \emph{CRaFH superalgebras}, which are the cyclotomic quotients of the RaFH superalgebras. We construct bases for these superalgebras, and compute the Gram determinants of natural trace forms, and use these to determine when these superalgebras are symmetric or Frobenius. To study the representation theory of the CRaFH superalgebras, we introduce the \emph{respectable algebras}, which is a vast generalisation of cellular algebras, standardly based algebras and finite dimensional affine cellular algebras, and give many examples illustrating their variety and ubiquity. We then show that CRaFH superalgebras are respectable algebras with weight poset given by multipartitions that are coloured by the representations of the underlying Frobenius algebra. This result can be viewed as a far-reaching generalisation of Murphy's bases into the setting of CRaFH algebras.

papers.title: Recycled roots under reduction and descent in the Casas-Alvero problem
papers.abstract: For a Casas-Alvero polynomial $f$, the type of $f$ is one less than the minimal number of roots of $f$ needed to meet every Hasse derivative $H_1f,\dots,H_{d-1}f$. We show that the type does not increase under reduction modulo a prime and under the descent from degree $np^e$ to degree $n$ in characteristic $p$. Consequently, if no Casas-Alvero polynomial of degree $n$ and type at most $k$ exists over $\overline{\mathbb F}_p$, then none of degree $np^e$ and type at most $k$ exists in characteristic $0$, for every $e\ge 0$. For $k=2$ the hypothesis is equivalent to $p\nmid N_n$ for an explicit integer $N_n$, and we show by a finite computation that $N_n\ne0$ for $3\le n\le 22$ and $n=24$. In particular there is no counterexample of type at most $2$ in degree $24$. This gives infinite families of degrees for which the conjecture is not known and every counterexample has type at least $3$: the degrees $5\cdot 8009^e$, the degrees $6p^e$ for $21$ primes $p$ that are bad for degree $6$, the degrees $7p^e$, $8p^e$, $9p^e$ and $10p^e$ for $13$, $17$, $16$ and $103$ explicit primes $p$ that are bad for these degrees, and the degrees $20p^e$ and $24p^e$ for all primes $p$ outside a finite set (for $20p^e$, including $p=2^{31}-1$). For $k=3$ we obtain the first degrees in which every counterexample has type at least $4$: the degrees $6p^e$ for $p\in\{983,1901,51313000813080529\}$, the degrees $8\cdot397^e$, the degrees $9p^e$ for $p\in\{613,757\}$ and the degrees $10p^e$ for $13$ primes $p$.

papers.title: Regions of totally real arrangements of rational curves
papers.abstract: We prove a plane-curve analogue of Zaslavsky's theorem for arrangements of real rational curves for which every complex singularity with more than one local branch is real and all of its branches are real. If at least one component has odd degree, the number of real regions equals the total rational Betti number of the complexified complement. We also give a formula for bounded affine regions which records the number of branches at infinity and the connected components of the real affine curve. Oriented regions generate the middle Borel--Moore homology over $\mathbb{Q}$, and they generate it over $\mathbb{Z}$ when the component degrees are coprime. The relations are described by the circles in the real normalization and, in an affine chart, by winding functions. These results imply equality of combinatorial rank and real combinatorial rank in the framework of Brown--Dupont and Sturmfels--Telen. Examples include singular rational cubics, arrangements of conics, Chebyshev curves, and the plane model of the $27$ lines on a split cubic surface.

papers.title: Relative Rouquier linearity and inverse hybrid Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity
papers.abstract: We prove signed positivity for the expansion of a parabolic hybrid basis in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of a Hecke algebra. The coefficients have degree bounded by the length of the corresponding minimal coset representative. We deduce this linearity from Elias-Williamson's ordinary Rouquier linearity by a truncation argument. The result does not require the parabolic subgroup to be finite.

papers.title: Representations of Bound Quivers over $\mathbb{F}_1$ and Hall Algebras
papers.abstract: Representations of quivers over the virtual field $\mathbb{F}_1$ can be naturally extended to bound quivers with monomial and commutativity relations. In this paper, we introduce and study the Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ for a bound quiver $(Q,I)$ equipped with such relations. As in the quiver setting, $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ is a graded, connected, and cocommutative bialgebra, and the free subgroup generated by all indecomposable representations forms a Lie subalgebra. We study $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ in detail for two special classes of bound quivers: Nakayama bound quivers and gentle one-cycle bound quivers. In both cases, we prove that for any triple $L, M, N$ of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations over $(Q,I)$, the Hall number $g_{N,L}^M$ coincides with the evaluation of the corresponding Hall polynomial $\phi_{N,L}^M(t)$ at $t=1$. Consequently, there exists a canonical isomorphism between $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ and the degenerate Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_1(Q,I)$, justifying Tits's $\mathbb{F}_1$-philosophy in these settings.

papers.title: Search for a basis of the Temperley-Lieb algebra, using rewriting systems
papers.abstract: We begin by defining Temperley-Lieb algebra, in two different ways: as a presented algebra or as a diagrammatic algebra. Next, we look for a basis algorithmically, using rewriting theory. Finally, we introduce a generalization of the Temperley-Lieb algebra, which is an oriented version of the previous one. This pushes us to employ a more efficient tool, category theory, to use rewriting to easily obtain a basis for the algebra.

papers.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.

papers.title: Semiprojective Banach lattices
papers.abstract: We study a norm-controlled notion of semiprojectivity for Banach lattices, testing sequential quotient towers in separable ambient lattices and requiring arbitrarily small norm loss at a fixed stage. For a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space $X$, we prove that $C_0(X)$ is semiprojective if and only if $X$ is compact and an absolute neighbourhood retract. Finite $\ell_1$-sums preserve semiprojectivity, and arbitrary $\ell_1$-sums of $1^+$-projective lattices are semiprojective without any order-unit assumption. By contrast, $\mathbb{R} \oplus_\infty \ell_1$ fails to be semiprojective, showing that neither semiprojectivity nor $1^+$-projectivity is preserved by finite $\ell_\infty$-sums, extensions, or pullbacks over a projective base. Every separable semiprojective lattice is $\lambda$-projective for some finite $\lambda$, and its scalar-valued lattice homomorphisms separate points. Consequently, a separable reflexive Banach lattice is semiprojective precisely when it is finite-dimensional, and no nonzero separable atomless order-continuous lattice is semiprojective. We also characterise $\ell$-openness as $1^+$-projectivity relative to separable ambient lattices; for separable domains this is ordinary $1^+$-projectivity. The restriction to separable ambient lattices is redundant for separable domains but affects the nonseparable examples.

papers.title: Seshadri functions on surfaces
papers.abstract:
We study the Seshadri function on the ample cone of a smooth complex projective surface at a fixed point. At a submaximal class, we show that the function is differentiable if and only if there is a unique Seshadri curve. At a maximal class $L$, differentiability is equivalent to every curve $C$ computing the Seshadri constant satisfying $\frac{[C]}{{\rm mult}_x C}=\frac{[L]}{\sqrt{L^{2}}}$. We also prove that the non-differentiability locus is nowhere dense.
  For the blow-up of $\mathbb P^{2}$ at $r\ge 9$ very general points, assuming the $(-1)$-curves conjecture for the blow-up at $r+1$ very general points, we construct a non-empty open subset of the ample cone on which the Seshadri function at a very general point equals $\sqrt{L^{2}}$. Consequently, this function is not piecewise linear. Under the assumption of the Strong SHGH conjecture, we obtain a common non-empty open subset on which maximality holds at every point when $r\ge36$.

papers.title: Siegel-Weil type identities for general linear groups related to parabolic induction from two Speh representations
papers.abstract: We prove identities of Siegel-Weil type for Eisenstein series on general linear groups, attached to parabolic induction from two Speh representations corresponding to the same irreducible, cuspidal representation. Such an identity relates a residue, at a (simple) pole of an Eisenstein series, as above, to a value of a similarly structured Eisenstein series at a point of holomorphy.

papers.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar Groups
papers.abstract:
We study the singular loci of the reduced $\SL_2(\CC)$-representation varieties $R_{m,n}$ of non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar groups $B(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid b^{-1}a^m b=a^n\rangle$. We determine their dimensions and profile functions, which list the numbers of irreducible components in descending order of dimension. The components have dimensions three or five. Their reduced singular loci have the explicit description \[
  \Sing R_{m,n}
  =\left\{(\varepsilon I,Y):
  \varepsilon^m=\varepsilon^n,\quad
  (\tr Y)^2=\frac{(m+n)^2}{mn}\right\}, \] where $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ and $Y\in\SL_2(\CC)$. Each is a disjoint union of $\mu$ copies of the smooth affine quadric $Q=\{(x,y,z)\in\CC^3:x^2+yz=1\}$, where $\mu=2$ for $m-n$ odd and $\mu=4$ for $m-n$ even. Thus its complex algebraic isomorphism type depends only on this parity. Each quadric is homotopy equivalent to $S^2$, so the singular locus has integral homology $\ZZ^\mu$ in degrees zero and two and zero in all other degrees. An algebraic stratification gives its compactly supported E-polynomial $\mu(q^2+q)$, with $q=uv$. At every singular point, $R_{m,n}$ is locally analytically the product of a smooth surface and a nodal curve.

papers.title: Soluble subgroup pairs in symmetric and alternating groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every pair of soluble subgroups of the symmetric group $S_n$ or the alternating group $A_n$ has trivially intersecting conjugates whenever $n\ge21$. This answers the second question of Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness in Problem 21.3 of the Kourovka Notebook.

papers.title: Some applications of the Nygaard filtration and quasisyntomic descent in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This article gives an expository account of quasisyntomic descent and the Nygaard filtration in positive characteristic, complemented by several new applications to $p$-adic cohomology theories. The guiding result is a new approach to Illusie's comparison between fppf cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_p(1)$ coefficients and the slope $1$ part of crystalline cohomology. We follow work of Bhatt-Lurie, but give a more elementary presentation which does not rely on the formalism of $\infty$-categories. We then revisit Ogus' comparison theorem between infinitesimal cohomology and \'etale cohomology, and give new proofs of several results on fppf cohomology that were previously obtained with the de Rham-Witt complex. We also determine the action of multiplication-by-$n$ on the fppf cohomology of an abelian variety, answering a question of A. Skorobogatov to the author. This is an expanded version of the author's master thesis.

papers.title: Some Constructions in the Category of Topological Partial Actions
papers.abstract: We present some theoretical aspects of the categories of global and partial group actions of topological groups on topological spaces, denoted by G-ActTop and G-pActTop, respectively. We construct topological partial actions on products and disjoint unions of topological spaces, and G-pinvariant subspaces. Furthermore, we provide an adequate definition of congruence (G-pcongruence), which enables the construction of quotient objects in the category of topological partial actions. In addition, we associate a special G-pcongruence to each pair of strong G-pmorphisms. Then, we study products, co-products, equalizers, co-equalizers, pullbacks, and pushouts in the category G-pActTop. We find that the category of topological partial actions is finitely complete and contains a co-complete subcategory. Finally, we show that the relationship between a topological partial action and its enveloping action is functorial. As a consequence, we obtain that the categorical product in G-ActTop coincides with the categorical product in G-pActTop. Moreover, the envelope of a co-product in G-pActTop is given by the co-product of the respective envelopes.

papers.title: Spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We give a formula for the spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities. This is a revised version of a conjecture proposed by Steenbrink fifty years ago. Although this conjecture fails in the non-simplicial Newton polytope case, we can find the correction term using the intersection complexes and the primitive intersection cohomologies of toric varieties associated with non-simplicial compact faces. To verify the correctness of the formula, we provide a sample code for Singular which computes the spectral pairs and compares the output with that of sppairs in Singular for the three variable case.

papers.title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
papers.abstract: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus. In this paper, we give a combinatorial classification of $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in partial flag varieties. This is achieved by applying Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths forming crystal graphs of Demazure modules. Previously, Hodges and Lakshmibai classified $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in Grassmannians. $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in complete flag varieties were treated independently by Gao-Hodges-Yong and Can-Saha. Our classification generalizes and unifies these results.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds via Brill-Noether theory of curves
papers.abstract: Fix a polarised Calabi-Yau threefold $(X,H)$. We reduce a version of the Bayer-Macr\`i-Toda conjecture for $(X,H)$, which ensures the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$, to verifying a Brill-Noether-type inequality for curves on $X$. We then prove this inequality for a broad class of Calabi-Yau threefolds, including complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefolds in weighted projective spaces.

papers.title: The binary Collatz dynamics of the trinomials $x^n+x+1$: proof of two conjectures of Gallardo and Rahavandrainy
papers.abstract: Gallardo and Rahavandrainy studied an analogue of the Collatz map on $\mathbb{F}_2[x]$, in which $x(x+1)$ plays the role of $2$ and $x^2+x+1$ that of $3$: an odd polynomial $A$ is sent to the odd part of $1+(x^2+x+1)A$. They proved that every orbit reaches $1$, and conjectured that the orbit of the trinomial $x^n+x+1$ has length $2^s+1$, where $s$ is the largest integer with $2^{s+1}<n$, and that for $1\le t\le s-1$ it contains $2^t$ terms of the same degree. We prove both statements for every $n\ge3$. The proof rests on the identity $(x^2+x+1)+x(x+1)=1$: it reduces the dynamics to a map from one plateau to the next, characterises the last plateau of any orbit, and shows that along the orbit of $x^n+x+1$ the plateaus start at the $2^j$-th powers of the odd parts of the polynomials $x^m(x^2+x+1)+1$, the index $m$ following an explicit binary recursion. We also note that a later restatement of the conjecture, with a non-strict inequality, fails exactly when $n$ is a power of $2$. A script checks all the statements numerically.

papers.title: The category of nominal sets is locally monoidal closed
papers.abstract: The category Nom of nominal sets was proposed by Pitts and Gabbay as a setting for the semantics of abstract syntax with variable bindings. It is well-known that Nom is a topos, also known as the Schanuel topos, and in particular it follows that Nom is locally closed, i.e., every slice category Nom/X is cartesian-closed. In this paper, we show that Nom has a much stronger property: every monoidal (closed) structure on Nom induces a monoidal (closed) structure on all slice categories Nom/X. One monoidal closed structure of particular interest on Nom is the separated product A * B, whose right adjoint A -* B is called the separated function space. In particular, it follows that Nom is locally separatedly closed.

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: The Complete Intersection Discrepancy of a Curve II: Families of Curves
papers.abstract: We study equisingularity of families of reduced curves over smooth parameter spaces of arbitrary positive dimension, using the difference between two analytic invariants of a curve singularity: the multiplicity of its Jacobian ideal and its complete intersection discrepancy. This difference provides a fiberwise multiplicity criterion for Whitney equisingularity. We prove that Whitney equisingularity (equivalently, strong simultaneous resolution) is characterized by equidimensionality of the fibers of the exceptional locus of either the relative conormal space or the relative Nash blowup. We further show that this condition is equivalent to the emptiness of the relative polar variety of smallest dimension. In addition, we establish that the Milnor number of a reduced curve is Zariski upper semicontinuous. As an application, we show that the constancy of the Milnor number in a family of reduced curves is equivalent to its topological equisingularity, under a natural assumption on the fibers.

papers.title: The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky
papers.abstract:
We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties.
  We show that the base locus of the Gamma00 linear system on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold consists of 253 points, disproving the stronger version by Donagi and Beauville--Debarre of the Gamma00 conjecture of van Geemen and van der Geer. This also leads us to construct explicit indecomposable 7-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties that are not Jacobians, but lie in the so-called Big Schottky locus, thus disproving the corresponding conjecture from the Schottky-Jung approach to the Schottky problem.
  We furthermore show that while no even theta constant vanishes for the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, its associated Scorza quartic is identically zero.
  Finally, we show that there exist two different theta level (2,4) structures on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, for which the sets of second order theta constants are projectively equal. This disproves the expected injectivity of the second order theta constant map for all genera starting with 6.

papers.title: The dodecahedron web and its instanton homology
papers.abstract: For the planar dodecahedron web D, the octahedral diagram of instanton homology reduces the possible values of the SO(3) instanton homology to 60 and 64. The remaining choice is determined by three coefficients of a secondary map. We give a proposed proof that all three vanish and that the dimension is 64. We express the coefficients as counts of instantons on specified foam cobordisms with one-parameter families of metrics. The index calculation requires these instantons to have negative action. An estimate uniform under neck stretching excludes them when the perturbations are sufficiently small. The construction includes local Floer complexes with zero differential, the marking calculation for excision, and a simultaneous choice of regular perturbations compatible with the families. Exact matrices and the supporting foam calculations are provided separately.

papers.title: The Hankel determinants of an automatic sequence need not be automatic
papers.abstract: Allouche, Han and Niederreiter asked whether the sequence of Hankel determinants of a $d$-automatic sequence must be $d$-regular, or must become $d$-automatic after reduction modulo an integer. We answer the first question in the negative, and the second one for the reduction modulo $3$. Let $\alpha$ be the root of $f^4+f^2-Tf+1=0$ in $\mathbb{F}_3((1/T))$ with $|\alpha|<1$, the quartic of Mills and Robbins, and let $S$ be its coefficient sequence, which is $3$-automatic by Christol's theorem. The Hankel determinants of $S$ vanish in runs whose lengths are unbounded but of the order of the square root of their position, because the partial quotients of $\alpha$ are unbounded while its irrationality exponent is $2$; and a lemma of Schlage-Puchta forbids runs in that regime in an automatic sequence. Hence these Hankel determinants are $k$-automatic for no $k$, and the integer Hankel determinants of any lift of $S$ are $k$-regular for no $k$.

papers.title: The inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition for the Suzuki and Ree groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give verifications of the inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition in [8] for the Suzuki and Ree groups at all primes.

papers.title: The invariant $c_M$ of Gallardo and Rahavandrainy at Mersenne prime exponents, and the case $p=7$
papers.abstract: A Mersenne prime polynomial is an irreducible polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the form $x^a(x+1)^b+1$ with $a,b\ge1$. Gallardo and Rahavandrainy conjectured that, apart from two exceptions, $\sigma(M^{2h})$ always has an irreducible factor which is not a Mersenne prime. For a prime $p\ge5$ they proved it for every $M$ outside an exceptional set $\Sigma_p=\Sigma_p^1\cup\dots\cup\Sigma_p^4$, defined through an integer $c_M$ and an odd integer $m_M$ read off the leading coefficients of $\sigma(\sigma(M^{p-1}))$, and later they proved it for every Mersenne prime number $p\ge31$; their method does not reach $p=7$. We compute $c_M$ exactly when $p=2^d-1$ is a Mersenne prime number: $c_M=d+1$ if $\deg M\ne d$, and $c_M=d$ if $\deg M=d$. Consequently $\Sigma_p^1$ consists of the Mersenne primes of degree $d$ or $d+1$, $\Sigma_p^2$ is empty, and $\Sigma_p^3$, $\Sigma_p^4$ are described by $m_M=\deg M-d-1$ and $m_M=\deg M-d$ respectively. For $p=7$ this reduces the conjecture to the Mersenne primes $M$ with $m_M\in\{\deg M-4,\deg M-3\}$. A direct computation shows that $\sigma(M^6)$ has a non-Mersenne irreducible factor for every Mersenne prime $M$ of degree at most $500$, and that $m_M\le17$ in that range. Hence the conjecture holds whenever $7$ divides $2h+1$ and $\deg M\le500$, and a counterexample with $7\mid 2h+1$ would need $m_M\ge\deg M-4>496$. A script attached as an ancillary file checks these computations, and reproduces the table of exceptional sets of Gallardo and Rahavandrainy.

papers.title: The inverse problem for the number of connected induced subgraphs
papers.abstract: For a finite graph $G$, let $c(G)$ be the number of nonempty vertex sets that induce a connected subgraph. We show that a positive integer $k$ equals $c(G)$ for some finite connected graph $G$ if and only if $k\notin\{2,4,5,8,9,16\}$. Every attainable value $k\ne25$ is attained on $\lfloor\log_2 k\rfloor+1$ vertices, the least possible number, and $25$ needs six vertices. More precisely, for every $m\ge6$ each integer from $2^{m-1}$ to $2^m-1$ is the value of $c$ on a connected graph with exactly $m$ vertices. The proofs of these results are short and use no computer; computer calculations serve only as independent checks, and for two auxiliary results: the values on six to eight vertices, and the result on all connected subgraphs described below. The value $16$ falls into a gap above the path: a connected graph on $n\ge4$ vertices other than the path $P_n$ has at least $n-3$ more connected sets than $P_n$. The values $k\ge17$ are realized by a recursive construction from cones, disjoint unions and a family of graphs that we call near-cones, starting from seven small graphs; it produces a graph with $c(G)=k$ in time polynomial in $\log k$. The question arose from a problem of Ordoñez in continuum theory, through a reduction by Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez, who found the values up to $255$ by a computer search. The proof is formalized in Lean 4. We also observe that a theorem of Czabarka, Székely and Wagner on subtrees reduces the corresponding problem for the number of all connected subgraphs to a finite computation, and we report its outcome. We did not find these results in the literature, but we make no claim of novelty or priority.

papers.title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
papers.abstract: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.

papers.title: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic
papers.abstract: The present paper is an extended version of the lecture notes of a course given by the first author at the summer school on Formulas of Siegel and Weil (Bielefeld, September 2025). We survey three perspectives on the Siegel-Weil formula: classical, geometric, and arithmetic. We first recall the Siegel-Weil formula for elliptic theta series arising from positive definite lattices. We next discuss the higher genus case for lattices of arbitrary signature from an adelic viewpoint. After introducing orthogonal Shimura varieties, we present the geometric Siegel-Weil formula, in which the generating series of volumes of special cycles is shown to be an Eisenstein series. We conclude with the (partly conjectural) arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula, relating degrees of special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups to central derivatives of Eisenstein series.

papers.title: The Siriaisa Algorithm for Minimum Independent Dominating Set
papers.abstract: The Minimum Independent Dominating Set problem (MIDS) asks for a smallest maximal independent set of an undirected graph; unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, it cannot be approximated within $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. We present version 0.0.8 of \textsc{Siriaisa}, an ensemble of eighteen strategies that adapts the vertex cover algorithm \textsc{Salvador} and the independent set algorithm \textsc{Esperanza} to MIDS, with every exact subproblem a forest solved by a conditioned tree dynamic program. We prove that the output is an independent dominating set computed in $O((n+m)\,\alpha_{\mathrm A}(n))$ expected time, that its ratio is at most $\Delta$, that it is optimal on forests, and that its ratio is at most $\sqrt n$ on three classes of graphs. A degree-splitting strategy yields a dominating set of size at most $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor\,(i(G)+s(G))$ for an explicit splitting excess $s(G)$, which vanishes on bounded-degree families for large $n$ and is largest on complete graphs, where the output is optimal. More generally, splitting at $\lfloor n^{1-\varepsilon}\rfloor$ gives the bound $n^{1-\varepsilon}\,(i(G)+s_\varepsilon(G))$ for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$. We state the ratio $n^{3/4}$ as a conjecture whose proof would imply $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. Through a reduction of Chleb{\'\i}k and Chleb{\'\i}kov{\'a}, every output decodes into a vertex cover, with conditional consequences for the Unique Games Conjecture.
